properties.title: Jimmy Carter’s light at Leary, Georgia
properties.place: Outside the Lions Club meeting, Leary, Georgia
properties.shape: A bright light, as bright as the Moon, changing from white to blue to red and back
properties.summary: At about 7:15 one evening in 1969, Jimmy Carter was waiting outside a school lunchroom in Leary, Georgia, to speak to the local Lions Club, when one of the men pointed out a light in the west, about 30 degrees above the horizon. Carter said it seemed to come closer, stopped beyond the pine trees, changed from white to blue, then red, then white, and then receded, after 10 to 12 minutes. As governor, in September 1973, he filled in a sighting report for the International UFO Bureau, dating it October 1969; the Lions Club’s own records show his Leary speech was on January 6, 1969, and the club had disbanded before October. Investigators in 1976 found that most of those present did not remember the event. On January 6, Venus was a brilliant evening star in the direction Carter gave, which is the accepted explanation; Carter said later that he took it for something unexplained, not for a spacecraft.
properties.explanation: Robert Sheaffer and Allan Hendry identified it as Venus, which was near its greatest brilliancy in the western sky that evening; a later analysis proposed a barium-cloud release from a rocket fired at Eglin AFB. Carter himself said he never thought it was an alien craft.

properties.title: Fort Beaufort — police fire at an object
properties.place: Braeside farm near Fort Beaufort, Eastern Cape
properties.shape: Fireball that changed colour
properties.summary: Farmer Bennie Smit said he, his workers and local police fired shots at a fireball-like object that changed colour as it hovered among the trees on his farm. The story went around the world. Rumours said the army investigated the site but no records were produced. The town's "UFO Bar" and hotel clippings kept the story alive.

properties.title: Lake Cote aerial survey photograph
properties.shape: Metallic disc over the lake
properties.summary: An Instituto Geográfico Nacional aerial-survey camera flying at about 10,000 ft photographed Lake Cote for mapping. One frame shows a disc-like object over the water that the crew never saw; the adjacent frames do not show it.
properties.explanation: Taken by the government’s Instituto Geográfico Nacional mapping aircraft; the object was not noticed at the time. Analyses have not produced an accepted identification.

properties.title: Delphos ring
properties.shape: Mushroom-shaped, with multicoloured lights
properties.summary: While doing evening chores on his family’s farm near Delphos, 16-year-old Ronnie Johnson saw a mushroom-shaped object, lit in many colours, hovering about 25 yards away. His parents came out to a glowing ring on the ground where it had been. It was still visible the next day. Investigators found that the soil in the ring was dry beside damp ground and would not let water through, and that it held more calcium and soluble salts and was more acidic, with a white deposit of calcium oxalate. Both calcium oxalate and oxalic acid irritate skin and eyes, and Ronnie’s parents said touching the ring numbed their fingers. It is one of the classic UFO “landing trace” cases.
properties.explanation: No official body reached a conclusion. The soil results are the main physical evidence; sceptics note that the account rests on one family, and that fungi can leave rings of altered, water-repelling soil.

properties.title: Pascagoula encounter
properties.shape: Oval object with flashing blue lights
properties.summary: Charles Hickson and his young colleague Calvin Parker said that while fishing from a pier on the west bank of the Pascagoula River they heard a whirring noise, saw two flashing blue lights and an oval object about 30–40 feet across, and were taken aboard by three creatures with claw-like hands, examined and returned. They went to the Jackson County sheriff’s office around 11 p.m. Officers who suspected a prank left the two alone in a room with a hidden recorder; the men’s talk matched their story. The case set off a wave of 1973 reports along the Gulf Coast and made Hickson a long-time public speaker; Parker published his own account in 2018.
properties.explanation: No physical evidence was found beyond the two men’s testimony. Sceptics see a hoax or a hallucination; the witnesses stuck to their story, including when they were secretly recorded at the sheriff’s office.

properties.title: Coyne helicopter incident
properties.shape: Grey cigar-shaped body, red nose light, white tail light, green beam
properties.summary: An Army Reserve Bell UH-1H (tail number 68-15444) on its way from Columbus to Cleveland was cruising at 2,500 feet near Mansfield when the crew saw a red light closing on the helicopter from the east. Capt. Lawrence Coyne took the controls and began an emergency descent, expecting a collision. They then saw a cigar-shaped grey object hover over the helicopter, with a red light at the nose, a white light at the tail and a green beam that lit the cockpit. After it left, the crew found the helicopter at about 3,500 feet in a climb of 1,000 feet a minute, with the collective still fully down, and the compass spinning. The Army Reserve’s report is among the best-known official records of an aircrew encounter.
properties.explanation: The sceptic Philip Klass argued that the crew first saw a bright fireball of the Orionid meteor shower and then misjudged what followed. Investigators for CUFOS and others reject this: by their timeline the object was in view for several minutes, and a family on the ground reported lights too.

properties.title: Berwyn Mountains "crash"
properties.shape: Glowing light on the hillside
properties.summary: At 20:38 a loud bang and tremor shook villages around the Berwyn Mountains, and people saw lights on the hillside. A local nurse drove up and described a glowing sphere. Police searched and found nothing. The event was later retold as a UFO crash with a secret military recovery, sometimes called "the Welsh Roswell". Seismographs recorded an earthquake, and meteor observers logged a fireball at the same moment.
properties.explanation: A small earthquake shook the area at the same moment that a bright fireball was seen across northern England and Wales. The lights on the hillside were most likely poachers' lamps. Investigators found no crash and no recovery.

properties.title: Coyame “crash” — Chihuahua
properties.shape: Disc-shaped object (as told)
properties.summary: According to ufologists, residents near Coyame, in the Chihuahuan desert, reported a mid-air collision between a UFO and a small aeroplane on August 25, 1974, followed by a military recovery and a cover-up. The best-known version says U.S. air-defence radar followed a fast, high object from the Gulf of Mexico until it vanished near Coyame, and that a light aircraft that had left El Paso collided with it. Historians point instead to the real 1974 crash and recovery of a Cessna that had been carrying drugs, which they believe gave rise to the story. It is sometimes called Mexico’s Roswell. The case is listed because it is so often cited, not because the account is documented.
properties.explanation: Historians say the reports were most likely prompted by the crash and military recovery of a Cessna used for drug smuggling. The radar story that circulates in UFO literature is known only from later retellings.

properties.title: Langenburg rings
properties.shape: Five domed discs
properties.summary: Farmer Edwin Fuhr was swathing a rapeseed field when he saw five metallic, dome-shaped objects spinning just above the ground near a slough. He sat frozen for about 15 minutes until they rose silently in formation and left, trailing grey vapour. He said his swather would not restart. The RCMP found five rings of flattened, swirled crop matching his description, with no tracks leading in.

properties.title: Billy Meier’s “beamship” photographs
properties.place: Zürcher Oberland, around Hinwil, canton of Zürich
properties.shape: Disc-shaped “beamships” with domes and rings
properties.summary: Eduard “Billy” Meier, from the canton of Zürich, says that on January 28, 1975, he met Semjase, a woman from the Pleiades, beside her spacecraft, and that contacts which had begun in his childhood went on for years. From 1975 he produced hundreds of sharp colour photographs and some film of saucer-shaped “beamships” over the fields and woods of the Zürcher Oberland, later the basis of books, a following and the 1987 film Contact. Scientists, sceptics and most ufologists regard them as fraudulent. Investigators such as Kal Korff argued that models had been photographed close up or combined with landscapes; Meier’s former wife Kalliope said in 1997 that she had seen the models and that the stories were invented; Meier conceded that he had used models to re-create scenes; and pictures he presented as the aliens Asket and Nera were traced to performers on American television.
properties.explanation: A hoax. Meier’s former wife said in 1997 that the “beamships” were models made from household objects such as dustbin lids and carpet tacks; Meier admitted to Gary Kinder that he had used models to “recreate scenes”; and photographs of two “Pleiadian” women turned out to show dancers from the Golddiggers troupe on The Dean Martin Show.

properties.title: Loring Air Force Base intrusions
properties.place: Loring Air Force Base, Limestone, Maine
properties.shape: Low aircraft with a red light and a white strobe
properties.summary: On the evening of October 27, 1975 a security patrol at Loring Air Force Base, a Strategic Air Command base that held nuclear weapons, saw an aircraft with a red light and a white strobe approaching the north perimeter at about 300 feet. The base was put on alert and a ground sweep began. Over the next 40 minutes the object came within 300 yards of the restricted weapons storage area at about 150 feet, moving in ways described as helicopter-like, and no one could get a fix on it before it left toward Grand Falls, New Brunswick. Similar reports came from the base, and from other bases, for more than a week; Air Force messages about them were released under the Freedom of Information Act.
properties.explanation: The Air Force never identified the object; its messages from the base describe an unidentified, helicopter-like aircraft that evaded the ground sweep. No conventional aircraft was found.

properties.title: Wurtsmith Air Force Base and the KC-135 chase
properties.place: Wurtsmith Air Force Base, Oscoda, Michigan
properties.shape: One white light pointing down and two red lights at the rear
properties.summary: At about 10:10 p.m. on October 30, 1975, guards at Wurtsmith, a Strategic Air Command base on Lake Huron, saw an object with a white light pointing downward and two red lights at the rear. Minutes later security police reported an “unidentified helicopter” hovering low over the weapons storage area, and the base radar approach control picked up a target about 35 miles to the south-east. A KC-135 tanker flying nearby was asked to look. Its six-man crew, among them Maj. Frederick Pappas, saw lights and painted the object on their radar for about ten seconds, and followed it at about 2,000 feet north over Lake Huron and then south toward Saginaw Bay; each time they closed in it sped away, and Capt. Myron Taylor put its final speed at about 1,000 knots. Low on fuel, they broke off. The NORAD log recorded that the tanker “made both visual sighting and radar skin paint” and that contact was lost 25 nautical miles south-east over Lake Huron.
properties.explanation: The NORAD log called it a helicopter over the weapons storage area, but no helicopter was identified, and the tanker crew described an object that pulled away each time they closed on it. It is one of a series of intrusions at northern Strategic Air Command bases that autumn, including Loring and Malmstrom.

properties.title: Travis Walton disappearance
properties.place: Apache–Sitgreaves National Forest near Heber, Arizona
properties.shape: Glowing disc hovering over a clearing
properties.summary: A seven-man logging crew led by Mike Rogers was driving out of the forest after sunset when they saw a glowing disc over a clearing. Travis Walton got out and walked toward it, and the crew said a beam of light knocked him to the ground. They drove off in panic. When they came back he was gone. Police searched for five days. Walton then called his sister from a phone booth in Heber, saying he had been taken aboard. His story became the 1993 film Fire in the Sky.
properties.explanation: The crew passed some polygraph tests and Walton failed one. Philip Klass and Michael Shermer argued it was a hoax, with a motive: the crew was behind on a Forest Service contract, and an "act of God" could excuse the penalty. Walton maintains it happened.

properties.title: Malmstrom AFB — objects over the missile fields, November 1975
properties.place: Malmstrom Air Force Base and its Minuteman missile fields, Montana
properties.shape: Lights over the launch facilities; on radar, slow targets that sounded like a jet
properties.summary: In the first weeks of November 1975, after the intrusions at Loring and Wurtsmith, NORAD’s logs and messages record a run of reports from the Minuteman fields around Malmstrom AFB in Montana. Security teams at several launch facilities reported lights and objects; Malmstrom’s search and height-finder radars carried a target between about 9,000 and 15,600 ft moving at only seven knots; witnesses said it sounded like a jet, and the FAA said no jets were in the area. F-106 interceptors scrambled from Malmstrom could not make contact because of the darkness and the target’s low altitude. The NORAD messages, released under the Freedom of Information Act by 1979, give no explanation. Later accounts add a security alarm at launch facility K-7, a glowing disc “the size of a football field” and tampered warheads; those details come from interviews years afterwards, not from the released records.

properties.title: CFS Falconbridge — the NORAD message from Ontario
properties.place: 30 nautical miles south-south-west of Canadian Forces Station Falconbridge, near Sudbury, Ontario
properties.shape: A circular, brilliantly lit object with two black spots in the centre
properties.summary: At 11:15 UTC (6:15 a.m. local) on November 11, 1975, personnel at CFS Falconbridge, a Pinetree Line radar station north-east of Sudbury, saw and tracked an object bearing 210 degrees magnetic, 30 nautical miles from the station. 22nd NORAD Region Headquarters passed the report to the National Research Council in Ottawa: a “circular object, brilliantly lighted with two black spots in the center”, moving straight up “at high speed from 42,000 ft. to 72,000 ft.” with no horizontal movement, for 14 minutes, under broken cloud. The major who was the prime witness took photographs but did not know if they would come out. The same observers saw a similar object bearing 270 degrees, too far away for detail, and the Ontario Provincial Police in Sudbury received many other reports. The station’s history adds that two F-106 interceptors were scrambled from Selfridge Air National Guard Base in Michigan and saw nothing.
properties.explanation: No explanation was given. The sighting came in the autumn of 1975, when bases along the northern U.S. border were also reporting lights and radar targets. The radar fixed only a bearing and range; the height and the vertical climb are the observers’ estimates.

properties.title: CFS Falconbridge — the NORAD message from Ontario
properties.label: Object, from the NORAD message

properties.title: Canary Islands sphere
properties.shape: Light rising from the sea, then a huge glowing sphere
properties.summary: The crew of the corvette Atrevida saw a light rise from the sea, then a vast, luminous sphere spread out in the sky. Hundreds of people across Tenerife, La Palma, La Gomera and Gran Canaria saw it. A doctor near Gáldar said he saw two tall figures inside a transparent sphere. The Spanish Air Force investigation was leaked in 1977 and officially declassified in 1994.
properties.explanation: Spanish researcher Ricardo Campo matched the 1976 sighting, and similar Canary Islands events of the period, to U.S. Navy submarine-launched Poseidon missile tests in the Atlantic, whose exhaust clouds glow in sunlight at high altitude. The Spanish Air Force report left it unexplained.

properties.title: Tehran F-4 Phantom intercepts
properties.shape: Brilliant flashing lights; object released a smaller one
properties.summary: After civilian reports of a bright object over Tehran’s Shemiran district, the Imperial Iranian Air Force scrambled two F-4 Phantoms from Shahrokhi AB. Both crews said their instruments and communications failed near the object; the second pilot, Maj. Parviz Jafari, reported a radar lock and that his weapons panel died as a smaller object came toward him.
properties.explanation: A U.S. Defense Intelligence Agency report called it "an outstanding report" meeting all criteria for a valid study. Skeptic Philip Klass proposed Jupiter plus coincidental equipment failures.

properties.title: The Moroccan coast “UFO” — a Soviet rocket part re-entering
properties.place: Along the Atlantic coast of Morocco, from Agadir to Kenitra and inland to Meknes and Fez
properties.shape: A silvery, luminous flattened ball or a large luminous tube, shedding bright sparks from the rear
properties.summary: Between 1 and 2 a.m. on September 19, 1976, the Royal Gendarmerie took calls from Agadir, Marrakech, Casablanca, Rabat, Kenitra and other towns describing the same thing: a silent, silvery, luminous object, disc-shaped to some and tube-shaped to others, moving slowly from south to north parallel to the Atlantic coast and giving off intermittent trails of bright sparks and fragments. Major Mohamed Lissaoui of the Gendarmerie saw it himself at about 1:15 a.m. on his way back from Kenitra, flying low and slowly “as if it were an aircraft preparing to land”. King Hassan II sent the Gendarmerie’s commander, Col. Housni Benslimane, to the U.S. embassy on September 23 to ask what the Americans knew; the defence attaché was shown witnesses’ drawings and cabled Washington. The State Department answered that it knew of no U.S. aircraft or satellite activity and that a meteor or a decaying satellite was possible. The cables became public through WikiLeaks in 2013.
properties.explanation: In 2012 the satellite tracker Ted Molczan matched the time and track to the re-entry of a piece of a Soviet Molniya rocket (an ullage-motor assembly from the third stage that orbited Molniya 1-35 in July 1976), an object catalogued by U.S. space tracking. The State Department’s 1976 reply had already said the sightings “could conceivably be compatible with a meteor, or a decaying satellite”. The witnesses’ estimate of 1,000 m was far too low, as estimates of a re-entry’s height usually are.

properties.title: The Moroccan coast “UFO” — a Soviet rocket part re-entering
properties.label: Rocket part re-entering (approximate, from the witness reports)

properties.title: Talavera la Real air base sentries
properties.place: Talavera la Real Air Base, Badajoz
properties.shape: Intense light; tall luminous figure
properties.summary: Two soldiers on night patrol at Talavera la Real air base heard a sound like radio interference that became a piercing whistle. When it stopped they saw an intense light in the sky for about 15 seconds. With a third guard and a guard dog they searched the perimeter. The dog came back cowering, and they said they saw a tall, glowing figure and fired their rifles at it before it vanished. The Spanish Air Force investigated and later released its file.

properties.title: Broad Haven schoolchildren — the Welsh Triangle
properties.shape: Yellow cigar-shaped craft; later an “upside-down saucer”
properties.summary: At lunchtime on February 4, 1977 a group of 14 children at Broad Haven Primary School reported a yellow, cigar-shaped craft that landed in a field beyond the school grounds, and a silver creature with pointed ears. The headmaster had them draw what they saw, and the drawings agreed closely. On February 17 teachers and others said they saw the same craft, and on April 19 the owner of the Haven Fort Hotel in nearby Little Haven reported an “upside-down saucer” and two figures in a field. The wave of sightings in the area became known as the Dyfed or Welsh Triangle. A Ministry of Defence investigator found nothing to show a landing. The events were revisited in a 2023 Netflix documentary and a 2024 BBC series.
properties.explanation: A Ministry of Defence investigator found no physical evidence that anything had landed and suggested that “a local prankster” might have been responsible. The children’s drawings agreed closely, which is why the case is still told.

properties.title: Corporal Valdés — the patrol at Pampa Lluscuma
properties.shape: Bright violet lights descending from the sky
properties.summary: In the early hours of April 25, 1977, a Chilean Army patrol of a corporal and seven conscripts camped on the Pampa Lluscuma, in the altiplano near Putre, said two bright lights came down near them. Corporal Armando Valdés walked towards one and disappeared; about fifteen minutes later he came back, collapsed and said, “You don’t know who we are or where we come from, but I assure you we will return.” The soldiers said his face now carried several days’ beard and his digital watch showed a date five days ahead. The story reached the press across the world, from Chilean papers to French ones, and became Chile’s best-known UFO case. It was never investigated under the military government: no statement was taken officially and the watch was neither photographed nor studied. Later reporting found that the group was guarding army horses rather than patrolling, and some soldiers said Valdés had a beard before that night. Valdés has given contradictory accounts since, at times calling it a prank that got out of hand.
properties.explanation: Valdés himself said in later interviews (reported for 2004, 2009 and 2013) that it was a joke among the patrol that got out of hand, with the watch set forward and the beard explained away to avoid punishment for not shaving, though at other times he has said it happened. The army never investigated and the watch was never examined.

properties.title: Petrozavodsk phenomenon
properties.shape: Glowing "jellyfish" showering rays
properties.summary: In the early hours, residents of Petrozavodsk saw a glowing object spread over the city like a jellyfish, "raining" shafts of light. Reports came from across the Soviet Union and Finland. The event prompted the Soviet research programme Setka.
properties.explanation: Usually attributed to the launch of Kosmos-955 from Plesetsk, but the 1977 Academy of Sciences report said the phenomenon could not be satisfactorily understood.

properties.title: Colares "chupa-chupa" & Operação Prato
properties.shape: Beams of light, "chupa-chupa" lights
properties.summary: Residents of Colares reported lights that fired beams and left burn-like marks. The mayor asked for help, and the Brazilian Air Force ran Operação Prato under Capt. Uyrangê Hollanda, photographing lights over several months. Hollanda gave a dramatic interview two decades later.
properties.explanation: The Brazilian Air Force closed Operação Prato after about four months, reporting no unusual phenomena; its files and photos are in the Arquivo Nacional.

properties.title: The object that fell near Bermejo — Bolivia’s 1978 search
properties.place: El Taire hill above the Bermejo River, Tarija department, on the Argentine border
properties.shape: A luminous cylinder or egg with a flaming tail
properties.summary: In the afternoon of May 6, 1978 (some reports say the Sunday evening, May 7), people on both sides of the Bermejo River, where Bolivia’s Tarija department meets Argentina, saw a luminous object with a fiery tail fall towards the El Taire hill and heard an explosion and a sonic boom. The Bolivian army and police searched, scientists from the University of Tarija went to the area, Argentina sent border police, and newspapers in Buenos Aires carried a police chief’s description of a dull metal cylinder about four metres long. The U.S. Embassy in La Paz reported the fall to Washington, and two U.S. Air Force attachés flew to Tarija; the embassy denied any secret recovery. A CIA-released bulletin of May 17, 1978 is headed “Bolivia reports conflict on details of fallen object”. The searches, slowed by the terrain and weather, recovered nothing anyone published. Explanations at the time ranged from a meteorite to space debris; no country reported losing a satellite, no meteorite fall is catalogued there for that date, and the object was never identified.

properties.title: Emilcin abduction report
properties.shape: White, hovering, humming craft
properties.summary: Jan Wolski, a 71-year-old farmer, said that while driving his horse-drawn cart through the woods near Emilcin, two short beings with greenish faces invited him aboard a white craft hovering over a clearing. There they examined him. He was later interviewed by investigators, who found him sincere. A monument now stands near the site, one of the few UFO memorials in the world.

properties.title: Gujan-Mestras — the light that put out the street lamps
properties.shape: An orange, oval luminous object
properties.summary: On the night of June 19, 1978, several people in Gujan-Mestras, on the Arcachon basin, heard a loud, dull noise and then saw an orange, oval light over the town. While it was there the street lighting faltered; the light faded from view as it climbed. Motorists on the road to Bordeaux near La Réole also saw a light moving slowly in the stormy sky. The gendarmerie took statements and GEPAN, the French space agency’s UFO office, investigated. GEIPAN classes the case B: probably a weather phenomenon connected with the storm. The two sightings could not be shown to be the same thing.
properties.explanation: GEIPAN class B: the witnesses probably saw an atmospheric phenomenon linked to the thunderstorm threatening the area. The gendarmerie and GEPAN could not link the town sighting to a light seen by motorists near La Réole.

properties.title: Disappearance of Frederick Valentich
properties.place: Bass Strait, off Cape Otway, Victoria
properties.shape: "Long shape" with four bright lights, orbiting above
properties.summary: Twenty-year-old Frederick Valentich, flying a Cessna 182L from Moorabbin to King Island, told Melbourne Flight Service a large lit aircraft was orbiting over him. His last words were "It is not an aircraft", followed by 17 seconds of metallic noise. No trace of him or the aircraft was ever found.
properties.explanation: The Department of Transport could not determine the cause. Theories include disorientation (seeing his own lights reflected while inverted), a staged disappearance and suicide.

properties.title: Clarenville — RCMP constable watches object over the water
properties.shape: Oval with a fin, lights
properties.summary: In the early morning a dozen people in Clarenville called the RCMP about an object hovering over the water toward Random Island. Constable James Blackwood watched it for one to two hours through a surveillance telescope. He described an oval with a fin at the back, hanging about 100 ft above the water. When he flashed his headlights, the object seemed to flash back. It then vanished and left no trace.

properties.title: Kuwait’s oil-field sightings and the pumps that stopped
properties.place: Kuwait Oil Company fields around Umm al-Aish, near the satellite earth station, northern Kuwait
properties.shape: A dazzling light; close up, a domed disc the size of a jumbo jet with a red light on top
properties.summary: On the night of November 9–10, 1978, according to the Kuwaiti dailies Al-Qabas and Al-Watan, employees of the Kuwait Oil Company and of the satellite station near Umm al-Aish saw a dazzling light come down nearby. Four oil-company workers, one of them an American, went to within about 250 metres and saw a disc as big as a jumbo jet, with a cupola and a red light on top, which stayed on the ground for about seven minutes while telephone and radio links in the area were cut, then rose vertically at great speed. Sightings over the oil fields went on until December 14. The U.S. embassy’s cable to Washington in January 1979, “UFO sightings cause security concern in Kuwait”, reported that the government had set up a committee of experts from the Kuwait Institute for Scientific Research, and that a senior Kuwait Oil Company official said the oil-pumping equipment had shut down automatically during one sighting and started again by itself when the object left, although it could normally be restarted only by hand.
properties.explanation: The government’s committee of experts from the Kuwait Institute for Scientific Research ruled out spy aircraft but gave no explanation, and its report was never published. The U.S. embassy reported the stop and restart of the pumping equipment as a Kuwait Oil Company official described it; nothing else about the landing is documented beyond press accounts.

properties.title: Zanfretta — the Torriglia night patrol
properties.shape: Red oval craft over 10 m across; later a triangular craft
properties.summary: At about 11:30 p.m. on December 6, 1978 the 26-year-old security guard Pier Fortunato Zanfretta, on patrol at Marzano, in the municipality of Torriglia, noticed four lights in the garden of a mansion called Casa Nostra and then a red oval object more than ten metres across. He radioed his supervisor that “they are not men”, then contact was lost; he was found unconscious and in shock. He described three-metre beings with mottled skin, yellow triangular eyes and clawed feet. A semicircular imprint of flattened grass was found in the garden, and Carabinieri Brigadier Antonio Nucchi collected 52 statements from people who had seen strange lights that night. A neurologist found no mental disturbance in January 1979. Zanfretta later described further abductions, eleven in all between 1978 and 1981, which are the most disputed part of the story.
properties.explanation: Sceptics say the grass imprint matched the place where the owners tied a horse, that regression hypnosis can create false memories, that the beings resembled characters in popular 1978 Italian TV and comics, and that the “footprints” were puddles. Italy’s national UFO centre (CUN) judged the case unreliable.

properties.title: Kaikōura lights
properties.shape: Bright white lights with a red tinge; pulsing orb
properties.summary: After a Safe Air crew reported lights tracked by Wellington radar on 21 December, an Australian TV crew rode along on the Argosy newspaper run. On the night of 30–31 December they filmed lights pacing the aircraft off the Kaikōura coast in colour on 16 mm film, with Wellington controllers reporting matching radar returns.
properties.explanation: Explanations offered include Venus and Jupiter, squid-fishing boat lights, and meteors; none accounts for the radar returns to everyone’s satisfaction.

properties.title: Cecconi G.91R photographs over Treviso
properties.shape: Dull black, capsule-shaped, with a milky dome
properties.summary: Returning from a photo-reconnaissance sortie in a G.91R, Italian Air Force pilot Giancarlo Cecconi was asked to identify an object tracked by Istrana radar over Treviso air base. He found a dull black, capsule-shaped object about 6–8 m long at about 1,300 m. He made passes within about 100 m and took more than 80 photographs with the aircraft's reconnaissance cameras. Then radar and the tower both lost it.
properties.explanation: The Italian Defence Ministry later said its photo interpreters had identified the object as a cylindrical balloon made of black plastic bags (a "solar balloon"). Cecconi rejected this, noting the object did not move in his jet's wake.

properties.title: Pranles — the yellow light with a turning blue beam
properties.shape: A stationary yellow-orange light projecting a blue beam that turned through 360°
properties.summary: From 22:45 to 23:28 on July 21, 1979, a couple at Pranles, in the Ardèche, watched a stationary yellow-orange light on top of a ridge towards the Serre de Pieroulet, like a lighthouse, projecting a blue beam that turned steadily through 360° and swept the ground. No sound was heard. As the husband, a scientist who worked on light and colour, prepared to take a photograph, it went out. Their neighbours had seen the same light in the same direction before closing their shutters at about 23:00. He reported it to the gendarmerie the next day. Re-examining the case decades later, GEIPAN found that a helicopter with a searchlight was the only plausible explanation, but a blue beam from a yellow source, turning continuously for no purpose, did not fit it. The case stays class D, unexplained, though GEIPAN notes it is near the line between unexplained and unusable because no field investigation was made at the time.

properties.title: Val Johnson — deputy's patrol car struck by a light
properties.shape: Beam of bright light just above the road
properties.summary: Deputy Val Johnson was patrolling rural roads when he saw a bright light just above the road. It rushed toward his car, the car was engulfed in light, and he heard glass breaking. He said he was unconscious for 39 minutes. Deputies found the car skewed across the road. The windshield was cracked, a headlight and the roof light were broken, and an aerial was bent. Both his watch and the car's clock were 14 minutes slow. A doctor compared his eye irritation to "welder's burns".
properties.explanation: UFO researchers (Allan Hendry, Jerome Clark) consider it significant. Skeptic Philip Klass argued it was a hoax and that Johnson damaged the car himself. The patrol car is on display at the Marshall County museum.

properties.title: Dechmont Law — Robert Taylor
properties.shape: Dome-shaped object; two spiked spheres
properties.summary: Forestry worker Robert Taylor walked into a clearing on Dechmont Law and saw a large dome-shaped object hovering. He said two smaller spiked spheres rolled out, grabbed his trousers and dragged him toward it, and he passed out. He came to with torn trousers, grazes and a headache, and staggered home. Police recorded the case as an assault and found marks in the ground. It is often described as the only UFO event police have investigated as a crime. A marker now stands at the site.

properties.title: Manises — airliner diversion & Mirage intercept
properties.shape: Red lights on a collision course; truncated cone
properties.summary: TAE flight JK-297 from Salzburg (via Palma) to Las Palmas saw red lights approach on a collision course near Ibiza and track the aircraft after it changed altitude. The captain diverted to Valencia — the first airliner diverted by a UFO. A Mirage F1 from Los Llanos then chased lights that accelerated away.
properties.explanation: Spanish Air Force files declassified in the 1990s did not confirm an anomalous object; researchers attribute the lights to refinery flare stacks and bright stars/planets.

properties.title: Cergy-Pontoise “abduction” (hoax)
properties.shape: A light over the road that wrapped the car in fog and small flashing spheres
properties.summary: Before dawn on November 26, 1979, a young man telephoned the police at Cergy-Pontoise to say his friend had been “abducted by a UFO”. Three friends said they had been loading jeans to sell at a market when a light appeared over the road; the driver went towards it, it wrapped the car in fog and small flashing spheres, and when the fog cleared he was gone. Seven police officers and gendarmes searched; the story became national news. The missing man reappeared at a friend’s flat on December 3, with a journalist present, saying he had woken in a cabbage field. GEPAN’s technical note found that the witnesses’ accounts diverged from the start, that a blood test gave no sign of time in weightlessness, and that cabbages said to have been dried by the light had been left to rot as fertiliser by their owner. GEIPAN classes the affair as a hoax.
properties.explanation: A hoax. GEIPAN, which reviewed the police and gendarmerie inquiry and its own analyses, calls it “a hoax whose course discredits the scientific work”; one of the friends is reported to have admitted years later that he made the story up.

properties.title: La Joya air base pursuit
properties.place: La Joya air base, Arequipa, Peru
properties.shape: Large balloon-shaped object
properties.summary: On the morning of April 11, 1980 about 1,800 people at the La Joya base saw a large, balloon-shaped object hanging still at around 500 metres. Lt Oscar Santa María Huertas, 23, took off in a Sukhoi Su-22 and fired 64 rounds at it without effect. He reported that it climbed away at up to 950 km/h, reaching about 19,200 metres, and stopped so suddenly that he had to swerve to avoid it. Peruvian army radar was said to show only his aircraft, while operators saw the object by eye. The engagement is said to have lasted 22 minutes, until his fuel ran low. The Peruvian Air Force kept the matter classified for decades; U.S. defence documents titled “UFO sighted in Peru” have since been released.
properties.explanation: Peru’s air force kept the case quiet for decades; no explanation has been published. Peru has since set up an office (now DIFAA) for aerial anomalies, and U.S. documents on the case were later released.

properties.title: Todmorden — PC Alan Godfrey
properties.shape: Diamond-shaped object hovering over the road
properties.summary: Before dawn, PC Alan Godfrey was driving his patrol car along Burnley Road looking for missing cattle when he found a large, diamond-shaped object hovering about 5 ft above the road, blocking it. He sketched it from the car. The next thing he knew, he was farther down the road and some time had passed. He said the road surface under the object was dry though the rest was wet. Other officers reported a light in the sky that night. Later hypnosis sessions produced an abduction account.

properties.title: Rendlesham Forest
properties.place: Rendlesham Forest, outside RAF Woodbridge, Suffolk
properties.shape: Metallic lit object in the forest; star-like lights
properties.summary: USAF security patrols at the east gate of RAF Woodbridge saw lights descend into the forest and went in to investigate. Two nights later deputy base commander Lt. Col. Charles Halt led a team that took radiation readings at three ground depressions and recorded his observations on a micro-cassette. His memo to the MoD is one of the most famous UFO documents in Britain.
properties.explanation: The Ministry of Defence found no threat and did not investigate further. Skeptics attribute the lights to a fireball, the Orford Ness lighthouse (visible through the trees in the same direction) and bright stars.

properties.title: Cash–Landrum incident
properties.shape: Diamond-shaped object venting flame; escorted by ~23 helicopters
properties.summary: Driving home through the pine woods north-east of Houston, Betty Cash and Vickie Landrum with her grandson said a blazing diamond-shaped object hovered over the road, radiating heat. As it rose, they counted about two dozen helicopters, many resembling CH-47 Chinooks. All three reported injuries afterwards, and they sued the U.S. government.
properties.explanation: Army and Air Force inquiries found no helicopters or craft that matched; the witnesses’ lawsuit against the U.S. government was dismissed in 1986. Skeptics question the medical and helicopter claims.

properties.title: Trans-en-Provence landing trace
properties.shape: Lead-grey disc, two stacked saucers
properties.summary: Renato Nicolaï heard a whistle and saw an object land briefly on his terrace and fly off. The Gendarmerie took samples within a day; GEPAN’s laboratory analysis of the 2.4 m circular mark reported soil heated to 300–600 °C and chlorophyll changes in alfalfa leaves.
properties.explanation: The French government’s GEPAN (now GEIPAN, part of CNES) analysed soil and plant samples and reported heating and biochemical changes it could not attribute to a known cause. Skeptics suggest a vehicle or the witness.

properties.title: The spiral over south-west China
properties.place: Sichuan and Yunnan, and across south-west, north-west and south-central China
properties.shape: A star-like point that brightened and grew a spinning, silver, spiral-shaped band of light
properties.summary: At 10:38 p.m. on July 24, 1981, on a clear, moonless night, people across Sichuan, Yunnan, Gansu and neighbouring provinces saw a bright, star-like point grow brighter, begin to oscillate and develop a cloud-like band of light that turned into a huge silver spiral, spinning as it crossed the sky slowly from east to west. It was in view for six or seven minutes. The sighting started a nationwide craze for UFOs in the newly opened China; the U.S. Air Force’s Foreign Technology Division translated a Hangtian article about it, “UFO incident causes sensation throughout half of China”, which weighed a meteor, an aircraft and a flying saucer. Liu Yan, the Purple Mountain Observatory astronomer who handled many of the letters the public sent about UFOs in the 1980s, made it the subject of his first article on them and concluded it was man-made.
properties.explanation: Newspapers first quoted astronomers blaming a meteor shower; the astronomer Liu Yan of the Purple Mountain Observatory, who analysed the eyewitness reports, concluded it was a man-made object about 650 km up, and an article in the space magazine Hangtian put it at about 500 km and rejected the meteor idea. A slowly turning spiral of light seen from half a country is what a rocket stage venting propellant in sunlight looks like (compare the Norwegian and Australian spirals), but no launch has been matched to this one.

properties.title: Hannah McRoberts’ photograph — Vancouver Island
properties.place: A provincial park by the Eve River bridge on Highway 19, near Kelsey Bay, Vancouver Island, British Columbia
properties.shape: A sharply focused, domed disc against clear blue sky above a mountain peak
properties.summary: At about 11 a.m. on October 8, 1981, Hannah McRoberts photographed a mountain peak from a provincial park off Highway 19 near Kelsey Bay, on the north-east coast of Vancouver Island, while travelling with her husband and young daughter. Nobody noticed anything in the sky. When the film was developed days later, one frame showed a sharply focused, dark, domed disc above the peak. Richard Haines, a perception scientist at NASA Ames, examined the original negative with micro-densitometry and computer enhancement, visited the site and interviewed the family; he found no evidence of a hoax, concluded the object was three-dimensional and at least 30 feet away, and presented the photograph to the 1997 Sturrock panel on UFO evidence. It is still one of the most reproduced UFO photographs, and one of the most argued over.
properties.explanation: The NASA scientist Richard Haines examined the negative in 1987 and found no sign of tampering or a support thread; his measurements put the disc at least 30 feet from the camera, and interviews and a site survey supported the family’s account. Because nobody saw the object, a thrown object (a Frisbee, a hubcap or a pan lid have been suggested) cannot be ruled out, and later re-analyses from prints rather than the negative leave the case open.

properties.title: Brest-Guipavas airport — the fireball by the runway
properties.shape: A red-orange ball, low on the horizon, that seemed to drop into a field by the runway
properties.summary: At about 7:55 on the morning of November 22, 1981, in early light, people in four separate groups near Brest-Guipavas airport saw a red-orange ball low over the horizon that seemed to fall into a field beside a runway and vanish; some saw sparks or a short trail. The airport’s firefighters, who watched it come down as if landing, alerted the control tower. The gendarmes, contacted the next day by the air traffic controller, took eight statements and searched; no trace was found. GEPAN’s original file recorded a radar echo at the time, which made the case a class D, unexplained. GEIPAN’s re-examination found that the radar centre had treated the echoes as insignificant and that the controllers had seen nothing abnormal, and reclassified it B: a meteoroid on a grazing path, seen almost head-on.
properties.explanation: GEIPAN class B: probably a meteoroid entering the atmosphere on a shallow path, seen nearly head-on, which explains the red-orange ball, the short, slow descent and the sudden disappearance. A radar “spot” first cited in the file was not supported: the controllers noted nothing abnormal.

properties.title: Trancrainville — gendarmes on the A10 and the lit-up ground
properties.place: A10 motorway near Trancrainville, Eure-et-Loir, north of Orléans
properties.shape: An indistinct bright mass in the sky, and a strongly lit patch on the ground
properties.summary: Between 4:35 and 4:55 a.m. on January 23, 1982, two gendarmes of the motorway patrol, driving south on the A10, saw an indistinct bright mass in the sky and a strongly lit area on the ground beneath it, which moved across pylons and hangars. They followed it for about 30 km, driving and stopping, losing and finding it again, and heard nothing even with the engine off; at the end only a glow remained to the east over the trees. The Orléans air base, 7 km away, had nothing flying and its radar had been off since the evening before, and the motorway operator’s staff had seen nothing. Re-examining the case, GEIPAN rejected planets (they cannot light the ground) and judged a helicopter with a searchlight above the cloud, then at 1,200–1,500 m, too unlikely for the equipment of the time. It is class D, unexplained, with the caveat that no field interview could be made.

properties.title: VASP flight 169 — the light that paced a Boeing 727
properties.place: Night flight from Fortaleza to Rio de Janeiro, first seen near Petrolina, Pernambuco
properties.shape: A bright light changing from red to orange, with a white and bluish centre
properties.summary: VASP’s night flight 169, a Boeing 727 (PP-SNG) under Captain Gérson Maciel de Britto, left Fortaleza at 01:50 on February 8, 1982 for Rio de Janeiro. About half an hour later, near Petrolina, the captain saw a light approach on the left and pace the aircraft. It changed colour between red and orange around a white and bluish centre, seemed to move above and below the airliner, and stayed with it past Belo Horizonte; at 31,000 ft the crew said a bluish light filled the cabin. Britto called the air-traffic and air-defence centre CINDACTA in Brasília, which had no traffic there, dimmed his lights and flashed his landing lights at it, and woke the passengers; one compared it to a mercury street lamp. CINDACTA later said its radar showed a return about eight miles from the aircraft, and crews of a Transbrasil and an Aerolíneas Argentinas flight reported seeing something. The light was lost in cloud over the Serra do Mar a few minutes before landing at Galeão. The case was examined in the Journal of Scientific Exploration in 2014, which concluded that the “object” was Venus, very bright in the eastern pre-dawn sky.
properties.explanation: A study in the Journal of Scientific Exploration (2014) concluded the light was the planet Venus, rising brilliantly before dawn and possibly distorted by an atmospheric mirage. The captain rejected that, saying he knew Venus and the Moon; a radar return the air-traffic centre reported near the airliner has never been documented in detail.

properties.title: VASP flight 169 — the light that paced a Boeing 727
properties.label: VASP 169 (approximate route and times)

properties.title: Morenão stadium sighting
properties.place: Estádio Morenão, Campo Grande, Mato Grosso do Sul
properties.shape: Unidentified lights
properties.summary: During a Brazilian championship match between Operário and Vasco da Gama, a crowd of more than 24,000 saw unidentified objects over the stadium. Players, including Cocada, and referee José de Assis Aragão described them. Among the spectators was Ademar José Gevaerd, who went on to become one of Brazil's best-known UFO researchers.

properties.title: Hessdalen lights
properties.shape: White, yellow or red floating lights
properties.summary: Lights have appeared over the 12-km Hessdalen valley since at least the early 1980s, peaking at up to 20 per week in 1981–84. Unusually, they have been measured: radar, spectra, magnetometers and a permanent camera station have recorded them, but their cause is still debated.
properties.explanation: Studied since 1983 by Project Hessdalen with an automated measurement station; hypotheses include combustion of dust from the valley’s ores, plasma, and piezoelectric effects.

properties.title: Hudson Valley "Westchester boomerang"
properties.shape: V / boomerang of coloured lights
properties.summary: For over a year residents of the Hudson Valley reported a silent boomerang or V of bright lights, sometimes "the size of a football field". Guards at the Indian Point nuclear plant reportedly saw it in June and July 1984, and a Brewster resident videotaped the lights on 24 July.
properties.explanation: State police and the New York Power Authority attributed the sightings to pilots flying Cessna 152s in tight formation from Stormville Airport with coloured lights — a hoax the pilots reportedly enjoyed.

properties.title: Aeroflot Tu-134 over Minsk — the light that became a cloud
properties.place: Over Minsk, Byelorussian SSR, on the flight to Tallinn
properties.shape: A yellow light that threw out rays, became concentric circles and then a green cloud
properties.summary: At about 4 a.m. on September 7, 1984, the crew of an Aeroflot Tu-134 flying from Tbilisi via Rostov to Tallinn saw a bright yellow light appear to their right over Byelorussia. It threw out beams strong enough, by one account, to light up the houses and roads below, changed into concentric circles and then into a glowing green cloud that seemed to follow the airliner. Co-pilot Gennady Lazurin sketched it, and Captain Igor Cherkashin called air traffic control, which reported a “double” return on radar; a second airliner flying the opposite way also saw it. The newspaper Trud published the story in early 1985, a rare UFO report in the Soviet press. Rumours that crew members of the second aircraft later died of illnesses caused by the encounter have never been substantiated. Western analysts matched the sketches to the plume of a missile launched that night.
properties.explanation: Western analysts tied it to a Soviet missile launch that night, whose rising plume and glowing exhaust cloud look much like the crew’s sketches: Jonathan McDowell’s launch catalogue lists a submarine-launched R-29R test on September 7, 1984, with a note (after James Oberg) naming it as the source of the sighting. The Soviet army newspaper Krasnaya Zvezda suggested light refracted by floating space debris.

properties.title: Dalnegorsk “Height 611” crash
properties.shape: Reddish sphere about 3 m across
properties.summary: On the evening of January 29, 1986 residents of the mining town of Dalnegorsk saw a reddish, silent sphere about three metres across flying from the south-east at some 700–800 metres, at about 15 m/s. It crossed part of the town and came down on Izvestkovaya mountain, known as Height 611, burning on the slope. Investigators reported tiny metallic droplets 2–5 mm across, and fibres in a tangle of metal, quartz and gold-coloured threads. In Russia it is often called the best-documented UFO crash, although the technical findings come mainly from the group that investigated it.
properties.explanation: Ball lightning and other plasma phenomena have been proposed. The reports of unusual metal fragments come mostly from the investigating group and have not been independently confirmed.

properties.title: Brazil’s "Official UFO Night"
properties.place: São José dos Campos – Rio de Janeiro – Goiás
properties.shape: Red, white and green lights; 21 radar plots
properties.summary: Controllers at São José dos Campos and radar across south-east Brazil tracked about 21 unknown contacts. Embraer’s founder, flying in, saw red lights; the Air Force scrambled F-5Es from Santa Cruz and Mirage IIIs from Anápolis. Pilots reported lights that kept their distance and targets that appeared behind them.
properties.explanation: The Air Force commander said "we have no explanation". The report declassified in 2009 described objects with speeds from hovering to supersonic and 90° turns.

properties.title: Torpo film
properties.shape: Two bright objects, one flashing and throwing sparks
properties.summary: A couple at a mountain farm near Torpo, with their son and friends, watched two bright objects in the evening sky, one moving dramatically, flashing and throwing off sparks. The husband filmed them. Ground Saucer Watch found no sign of a hoax, but said the apparent motion could come from camera shake and that the lack of reference points made the film inconclusive.

properties.title: Japan Air Lines Flight 1628
properties.shape: Two small lights and a huge "mothership"
properties.summary: A JAL Boeing 747 freighter on the Reykjavík–Anchorage leg reported three objects pacing it at 35,000 ft, including one Terauchi described as enormous. Anchorage controllers reported returns near the aircraft; the objects stayed with the plane through turns and descents until near Talkeetna.
properties.explanation: The FAA’s radar returns were later dismissed as clutter / a split image; Philip Klass argued the crew saw Jupiter and Mars. The FAA found the crew professional and rational.

properties.title: Gulf Breeze photographs
properties.shape: Cylindrical craft with a ring of portholes and a glowing base
properties.summary: Contractor Ed Walters gave the Gulf Breeze Sentinel five Polaroids of a glowing craft he said hovered near his home. Over six months he produced dozens more photos and video, and described being hit by a blue beam and seeing aliens. Researchers such as Bruce Maccabee backed the photos, and other residents reported sightings. After the model was found in 1990 and a reporter recreated the pictures, the case became a textbook example of a UFO photo hoax.
properties.explanation: Considered a hoax. In 1990 the new owners of Ed Walters's former house found a styrofoam model UFO in the attic that a reporter used to reproduce the photos almost exactly. A local teenager also said he had helped fake them. Walters said the model was planted.

properties.title: Ilkley Moor photograph
properties.shape: Small green humanoid; two-part silver craft
properties.summary: On the morning of December 1, 1987 Philip Spencer, a retired police officer, was walking across Ilkley Moor, between Ilkley and Keighley, when he said he met a small dark-green figure about 1.2 metres tall, with a large head and long thin arms. He took one photograph before it ran off, then saw a whitish, two-part craft rise from the moor with a loud hum. About two hours were missing from his journey, and his compass pointed the wrong way. A wildlife photographer said the figure matched no known animal and Kodak found no signs of tampering, but the US Navy optics specialist Bruce Maccabee called the image too grainy to test. Under hypnosis in March 1988 his story changed to one of being taken aboard and examined.
properties.explanation: Critics say the blurry photograph could show a person or a cardboard cutout, and ask why no picture of the craft was taken. Kodak experts found no sign of tampering, but the image is too grainy for firm conclusions, and the account changed under hypnosis.

properties.title: Knowles family encounter
properties.place: Nullarbor Plain, between Madura and Mundrabilla, Western Australia
properties.shape: Large glowing ball
properties.summary: In the early hours of January 20, 1988, the Knowles family were driving across the Nullarbor Plain in their station wagon when a bright light appeared ahead. They said a large glowing object pursued the car for a long time and finally came down on the roof; the car seemed to be lifted off the road, and the engine and voices changed as if time were slowing. Mrs Knowles said she reached out of the rear window, felt something soft and warm on the roof, and found her hand covered in black dust. When the car dropped back onto the road a rear tyre burst. The family reported it at Mundrabilla. It is one of Australia’s best-known close-encounter stories.
properties.explanation: No explanation has been established. The account rests on the four family members’ testimony and the physical details they described, and has been widely reported in Australia.

properties.title: Villa Urquiza Christmas sighting
properties.shape: Silver object
properties.summary: On Christmas Day 1988 a silver object crossed the Villa Urquiza neighbourhood of Buenos Aires, watched by thousands of people. The city airport reported an object heading west toward Avenida General Paz. It is often called Argentina's most spectacular UFO sighting.

properties.title: Kapustin Yar — the KGB file on a night of lights over a missile depot
properties.place: Military sites 30–45 km from Kapustin Yar, Astrakhan oblast
properties.shape: A disc 4–5 m across with a dome, glowing dim green, with a bright flashing light and a beam
properties.summary: Between 22:10 on July 28 and 01:30 on July 29, 1989, soldiers and officers at military sites 30 to 45 km from the Kapustin Yar missile range, described in the reports as a transmission centre and a rocket-weapons depot, reported unidentified objects. At the depot, Ensign Valery Voloshin and a private watched through binoculars for about two hours as a disc some 4–5 m across with a dome, glowing a dim phosphorescent green, hovered 20 to 70 m above the warehouses, flashed a bright light and swept a beam, moved silently in sudden jerks, and finally left towards Akhtubinsk. Other officers described flashes like electric welding, a “flying plate” or a cigar-shaped object, and an aircraft was said to have been sent up but kept at a distance. The written statements, with unit names blacked out, were among 124 pages of military and civilian reports that the KGB passed in October 1991 to Pavel Popovich, president of a Soviet ufological association; Komsomolskaya Pravda published them in 2003. They are first-hand military reports, but nothing shows that anyone examined them.
properties.explanation: The reports are in a package of 124 pages that the KGB sent to the cosmonaut Pavel Popovich in October 1991, with a covering letter saying that the KGB did not study UFO reports but passed on what it received. No investigation or conclusion accompanies them, and the original file was later said to have gone missing.

properties.title: Voronezh park landing
properties.shape: Large red sphere / oval
properties.summary: TASS reported that children in a Voronezh park saw a large red ball land and tall beings emerge. Soviet reporting of the case — unusual at the time — made headlines worldwide.
properties.explanation: Reported by the Soviet news agency TASS; later widely regarded as a children’s story amplified by the press.

properties.title: Pereslavl-Zalessky — the Soviet air defence report
properties.shape: A disc 100–200 m across with two pulsing lights on its sides
properties.summary: On the night of March 21, 1990, air-defence units of the Moscow Military District reported more than 100 visual sightings of an object near Pereslavl-Zalessky. At 21:38 Lt Col A. A. Semenchenko was scrambled to identify a target at about 2,000 m; he saw two flashing white lights and a dim silhouette against the lights of the town, and the target did not answer his identification interrogation. Other pilots and radar posts gave times, bearings and distances; one ground radar post reported a fast-moving shining object with red lights, followed by another with white lights. In Rabochaya Tribuna on April 19, Colonel General Igor Maltsev, chief of the Main Staff of the Soviet Air Defence Forces, published excerpts: a disc 100 to 200 m across with two pulsing lights, flying silently between 1,000 and 7,000 m, at two to three times the speed of a modern fighter, rotating and hovering. Maltsev said he was “not a specialist on UFOs” and could only correlate the data. It was the first time a Soviet commander of that rank described such a case in public; the underlying reports have not been released, and no explanation was published.

properties.title: Belgian UFO wave — F-16 intercepts
properties.shape: Dark triangle with bright corner lights
properties.summary: Beginning with a sighting by two gendarmes at Eupen on 29 November 1989, thousands of Belgians reported large, slow triangles with lights. On the night of 30–31 March 1990, after ground and radar reports, two Belgian Air Force F-16s from Beauvechain made nine interception attempts and obtained brief radar locks; the Air Force published its report openly.
properties.explanation: The Belgian Air Force report left the radar contacts unexplained; critics attribute the F-16 lock-ons to the other fighter and to Bragg scattering. The famous Petit-Rechain triangle photo was admitted to be a hoax in 2011.

properties.title: Calvine photograph
properties.shape: Large diamond hovering; a Harrier jet nearby
properties.summary: Two men walking above Calvine photographed a large, silent diamond-shaped object hovering while a military jet flew past. Their negatives went from the Daily Record to the Ministry of Defence and vanished. A surviving print surfaced in 2022 and was published worldwide.
properties.explanation: The MoD never explained it; proposed explanations include a rock reflected in water and a hoax. The photographers have never been identified.

properties.title: The “immense triangle” over France — a Proton re-entry
properties.place: From the Bay of Biscay across France to Alsace
properties.shape: Three main lights in a group, read by many as an immense luminous triangle, with sparks and smoke trailing
properties.summary: At about 7 p.m. on November 5, 1990, a slow procession of bright lights crossed France from the Bay of Biscay to Alsace. Gendarmerie stations were flooded with calls, and for more than a week SEPRA, the CNES unit then in charge, answered witnesses describing “an immense luminous triangle”; the astronaut Jean-Pierre Haigneré was among them, and technicians at the CNES balloon base at Aire-sur-Adour held a launch to watch. On November 8 NASA identified the re-entry of object 20925, the third stage of the Proton rocket that had put the Gorizont 21 satellite into orbit, and CNES confirmed its track across France. The case, which fell in the middle of the Belgian wave, is a standard example of how a known re-entry is reported as a structured craft.
properties.explanation: The re-entry of the third stage of the Soviet Proton rocket that launched Gorizont 21 (catalogue object 20925, 1990-094C), identified by NASA on November 8 and confirmed by CNES orbit specialists; GEIPAN classes the case A, fully explained.

properties.title: The “immense triangle” over France — a Proton re-entry
properties.label: Proton third stage re-entering (approximate)

properties.title: Montreal — lights over the Bonaventure Hotel
properties.shape: Ring of 8–10 bright lights; a huge round form
properties.summary: From 7:20 to 10:20 p.m., people on the rooftop pool deck of the Bonaventure Hotel and in the streets below watched 8 to 10 lights hanging in a circle above them, sending down bright white rays. Some described a huge round object behind the lights. Police officers attended, and the next day La Presse reported the sighting. It drifted slowly north and was never identified.

properties.title: Alitalia MD-80 near miss over Kent
properties.shape: Brown, missile-shaped object
properties.summary: At about 8 p.m. on April 21, 1991, an Alitalia MD-80 flying from Milan to Heathrow with 57 people aboard was at 22,000 feet over the army ranges at Lydd, on the Kent coast, when Capt. Achille Zaghetti saw a brown, missile-shaped object pass about 1,000 feet above the airliner and shouted “Look out, look out”. The London control centre told him it had an unknown target on radar 10 nautical miles behind him. The Ministry of Defence and the Civil Aviation Authority investigated as an airmiss, ruled out a missile, a weather balloon and a rocket, and closed the case unsolved.
properties.explanation: The Civil Aviation Authority and the Ministry of Defence looked at missiles, weather balloons and rockets and ruled each one out, then closed the inquiry without an answer. The files were released by the National Archives in October 2008.

properties.title: Alitalia MD-80 near miss over Kent
properties.label: Alitalia MD-80 (approximate)

properties.title: Mexico City eclipse videos
properties.shape: Metallic disc or bright point, sometimes with a wavy haze
properties.summary: Millions in Mexico watched the total solar eclipse of July 11, 1991, with totality in Mexico City at 13:24 and lasting more than six minutes. At least 16 photographers and videographers recorded a bright, disc-like object near the Sun in the sky, some with a wavy trail of haze behind it. The sightings were widely seen on television and the case is a classic in Mexican ufology. Astronomers pointed out that the darkness of totality shows Venus, which stood a few degrees from the star Regulus, and that other planets also come into view, which fits many of the videos but not necessarily the apparent motion some of them show.
properties.explanation: Astronomers identified the brightest object as Venus (with Mars and Regulus nearby), made visible by the darkness of totality. Reflections in glass, camera artefacts and hoaxes account for others; not every video has been explained.

properties.title: Crop circles — Doug Bower and Dave Chorley own up
properties.place: The fields of Hampshire and Wiltshire; their first circles near Cheesefoot Head, Winchester
properties.shape: Circles of flattened cereal crop, later rings and complex patterns
properties.summary: From the late 1970s, circles of flattened wheat and barley appeared each summer in the fields of southern England, especially Hampshire and Wiltshire. By the late 1980s they were a national story, explained as UFO landing marks (“saucer nests”), as plasma vortices by the meteorologist Terence Meaden, and as messages by a new class of “cerealogists”. In September 1991 two men from Southampton, Doug Bower and Dave Chorley, told the newspaper Today that they had made circles since 1978, inspired by the 1966 Tully “saucer nest” in Australia, starting near Cheesefoot Head, and claimed more than 200 of them. They showed their tools, a plank, a rope and a cap with a wire loop to keep a straight line, and made a circle for journalists that the cerealogist Pat Delgado then declared authentic. Not every circle since is theirs, but none has been shown to have any cause other than people.
properties.explanation: Made by people. Doug Bower and Dave Chorley showed how they had made circles since 1978 with a plank, rope and a cap with a wire sighting loop, made one for journalists that a leading “cerealogist” declared genuine, and inspired the teams who make the elaborate designs today.

properties.title: Cosford incident
properties.place: RAF Cosford and RAF Shawbury, Shropshire
properties.shape: Triangular craft; lights in formation
properties.summary: Over the night of March 30–31, 1993, police officers, RAF personnel and the public across England and Wales reported lights in formation and a large triangular craft. A patrol at RAF Cosford saw it pass over the base. At RAF Shawbury a meteorological officer described a huge craft moving slowly across the airfield and sweeping a light beam over the ground. The MoD's Nick Pope pressed the case internally, and the files were later released to The National Archives.
properties.explanation: Most of the evening reports matched the re-entry of the rocket body that had launched the Russian satellite Cosmos 2238. The MoD found no threat. Nick Pope, who investigated for the MoD, argued that later reports, including a meteorological officer's at RAF Shawbury, were never explained.

properties.title: Air France 3532 — radar-visual over Coulommiers
properties.shape: Huge brown or dark-red disc or bell that seemed to change shape
properties.summary: At 13:14 on January 28, 1994, the crew of Air France flight 3532, an Airbus A320 from Nice to London, was cruising at about 11,900 metres near Coulommiers, east of Paris, when the chief steward and both pilots saw a huge object, like a brown bell or disc, off to the left. It seemed to change shape, stayed in view for about a minute and then vanished abruptly. Reims air traffic control had no traffic there, but the military radar at Cinq-Mars-la-Pile recorded a track for about 50 seconds that crossed the airliner’s path and disappeared at the same moment the crew lost sight of the object. The radar return and the crew’s description do not agree on distance or side, which is part of why the case remains open.
properties.explanation: GEIPAN, the French space agency’s UAP office, classes the case as unexplained after investigation. The military radar track is real but does not match the crew’s account closely: the crew saw a stationary object far off to the left, while the radar target was about a mile to the right and moving. Both vanished at the same moment.

properties.title: Lake Michigan lights — 911 calls and a weather radar
properties.place: The Lake Michigan shore of Ottawa and Muskegon counties, Michigan (Grand Haven to Holland)
properties.shape: Five or six round or cylindrical objects with red, green, blue and white lights, like flickering Christmas lights
properties.summary: On the night of March 8, 1994, dozens of people along the Lake Michigan shore of western Michigan called 911 about lights over the lake: five or six objects with red, green, blue and white lights that hovered and moved erratically. Police officers saw them too. A dispatcher called the National Weather Service office at Muskegon County Airport, and the meteorologist on duty, Jack Bushong, turned the office’s WSR-74C weather radar on the area and saw several returns where none should be, which he said moved fast and changed direction; he reported it to the National UFO Reporting Center. Days later the Weather Service played the radar down, saying it was built to see rain, not aircraft. Over the following weeks more than 300 people in 42 Michigan counties reported sightings; MUFON investigators interviewed dozens and found no explanation. Bushong kept his account for decades, and the case stays one of the better-documented police and radar cases of the 1990s.

properties.title: Ariel School, Ruwa
properties.shape: Silver craft landing in scrub; small beings
properties.summary: During morning break, 62 children said a silver craft landed in bush beside the playground and one or two small figures in black watched them. Their drawings were collected within days, and Harvard psychiatrist John Mack interviewed them.
properties.explanation: Skeptics suggest mass suggestion after a meteor/re-entry seen across southern Africa two days earlier; many former pupils still stand by their accounts.

properties.title: British Airways 5061 near miss over the Pennines
properties.place: About 8 nautical miles south-east of Manchester Airport
properties.shape: Wedge-shaped object with small white lights and a black stripe
properties.summary: At 18:48 on January 6, 1995, British Airways flight 5061, a Boeing 737 from Milan with 60 passengers aboard, was descending through about 4,000 feet over the Pennines toward Manchester when both pilots saw a lighted object pass very close down the right side, going the other way. They described it as wedge-shaped, with small white lights and a black stripe; the first officer ducked as it went by. Nothing showed on radar. The Joint Airmiss Working Group studied the report and, unable to identify the object, called it “unassessable”.
properties.explanation: The Civil Aviation Authority’s Joint Airmiss Working Group could not identify the object and rated the airmiss “unassessable”. No other aircraft or balloon was found, and no radar return was seen.

properties.title: British Airways 5061 near miss over the Pennines
properties.label: British Airways 5061, Boeing 737 (approximate)

properties.title: British Airways 5061 near miss over the Pennines
properties.label: Object (approximate)

properties.title: America West Flight 564 over the Texas Panhandle
properties.place: Over Bovina, Texas, near the New Mexico border
properties.shape: A row of white lights flashing in sequence; a long, dark, cigar-shaped silhouette against lightning
properties.summary: On the night of May 25, 1995, America West Flight 564, a Boeing 757 flying west at 39,000 ft from Tampa to Las Vegas, was passing over Bovina in the Texas Panhandle when the first officer, John Waller, and a flight attendant saw a row of bright white lights off to the right and below, flashing in sequence from left to right. When lightning lit the thunderclouds behind it, the crew saw a dark, wingless, cigar-shaped silhouette, which they estimated at 300 to 400 ft long, though its distance was unknown. Waller asked Albuquerque Center about traffic; the controllers had nothing on their radar and called NORAD, which reported a track that later proved to be a small aircraft with a faulty transponder. The next morning a controller said NORAD had tracked another target that stopped and accelerated repeatedly, but that was never confirmed. Walter Webb investigated for the Fund for UFO Research, interviewed the crew and the controllers and obtained the FAA tapes, and found no explanation; the SETI astronomer Seth Shostak later remarked that bright planets fool trained pilots, without analysing this case.

properties.title: Bariloche — the blackout and Aerolíneas Argentinas 674
properties.place: San Carlos de Bariloche airport, Río Negro, Argentina
properties.shape: A light between white and amber, like a star but much larger; later described as green and white, about 30 m across
properties.summary: At about 8:15 p.m. on July 31, 1995, Aerolíneas Argentinas flight 674, a Boeing 727 from Buenos Aires under Capt. Jorge Polanco, was coming in to land at Bariloche when the airport lost power, and then the whole city went dark as the airliner neared the runway, forcing a go-around. A light “between white and amber”, like a star but much larger and brighter, then flew on a parallel course about 100 metres from the plane. When the power came back the 727 climbed to 3,000 metres, descended and landed, and the light left at full speed toward the south-east. The tower chief and the crew of a Gendarmería Cheyenne flying 600 metres higher saw it too, and the tower’s instruments swung from one direction to another for no clear reason. Interviewed in 2026, Polanco said: “It pursued us, accompanied us for 17 minutes.”
properties.explanation: No explanation was found. Carlos Angueira, president of a local astronomy association, rejected a meteorite or a refraction, saying such things cannot “stop in the middle of the sky”. The case drew new attention in 2026, when it appeared among the Latin American incidents in UAP files released by the Pentagon.

properties.title: Bariloche — the blackout and Aerolíneas Argentinas 674
properties.label: Aerolíneas Argentinas 674, Boeing 727 (approximate)

properties.title: Varginha "ET"
properties.shape: Crouching humanoid with red eyes
properties.summary: Three young women said they saw a strange creature crouched near a wall, with vein-like marks on its skin, three bumps on its head and eyes like "two red balls". Rumours followed of military trucks carrying captured beings, bodies at hospitals, a police officer's death and animal deaths at the zoo. It became Brazil's best-known UFO story and a local tourist theme.
properties.explanation: A Brazilian Army inquiry concluded that the women had seen a local man with a mental disability, known as "Mudinho", and that the military movements were routine.

properties.title: Pretoria police helicopter chase
properties.shape: Bright, colour-changing light
properties.summary: At 4 a.m., Sgt Nico Stander of the Adriaan Vlok police station in Pretoria reported lights in the sky, which were videotaped. Some 200 officers and a Bo-105 police helicopter followed them east. The helicopter gave up at about 10,000 ft over the Cullinan area when it ran low on fuel. The lights were seen again on the nights of August 31 and September 1.

properties.title: The Wash incident
properties.shape: Rotating, multicoloured light
properties.summary: In the early morning a police officer on the Lincolnshire coast reported a rotating, multicoloured object over The Wash. The Claxby air traffic control radar reported a return in the same area. The report went up through RAF Kinloss and MoD Northwood before the conventional explanation was accepted.
properties.explanation: The radar returns were at least partly explained as echoes from St Botolph's Church ("the Boston Stump"), and the visual sightings as stars and planets.

properties.title: Phoenix Lights
properties.shape: Huge V / carpenter’s square with five lights
properties.summary: A V-shaped formation of lights was reported moving south-east from the Nevada line, over Prescott Valley and Phoenix to Tucson. Later that night a stationary row of amber lights was widely filmed over Phoenix. The event remains one of the most-witnessed UFO events in U.S. history.
properties.explanation: The ~20:00–20:45 V-formation was traced to A-10 aircraft of Operation Snowbird returning to Davis-Monthan AFB; the ~22:00 row of lights filmed over Phoenix were LUU-2 flares dropped over the Barry Goldwater Range. Some witnesses, including then-governor Fife Symington, reject this.

properties.title: Howden Moor — sonic booms and the search for a crash
properties.place: Howden Moors, Dark Peak, on the Derbyshire–South Yorkshire border
properties.shape: A large low aircraft with lit windows, a dark triangle, two red lights, then an orange glow and smoke
properties.summary: Shortly before 10 p.m. on March 24, 1997, people around the moors north-west of Sheffield saw low aircraft and heard explosions. Near Bolsterstone, Special Constable Marie-France Tattersfield and her husband saw a large aircraft with all its windows lit cross in front of them at no more than about 500 ft; a farmer saw a low plane head towards the moor, then an orange glow and plumes of smoke; gamekeepers heard “a terrific explosion”; others described a dark triangle or two red lights. Seismic and acoustic instruments of the British Geological Survey recorded two sonic events, at 21:52 and 22:06. Fearing an air crash, South Yorkshire Police led one of the largest searches in the region’s history: police and RAF helicopters and about 141 mountain-rescue volunteers searched up to 50 square miles of moorland for some 15 hours and found nothing.
