The Ministry of Defence first said no RAF aircraft was responsible, then admitted that six Tornados had been on low-flying training until 21:30, denied that any had gone supersonic, and closed the case after an RAF Police inquiry with “no military link”. The booms remain unattributed.
properties.explanation: The British Geological Survey said the recorded signal was atmospheric, not an impact, and most likely a supersonic aircraft. The MoD admitted a low-flying exercise by six RAF Tornados that it said had ended at 21:30, and denied any supersonic flight; an RAF Police inquiry in 1998 found no military link and suggested a natural cause such as a re-entry. The researcher David Clarke argues that a covert military flight continued after the exercise.

properties.title: Southern Illinois police sightings
properties.shape: Huge triangle / "arrowhead" with bright lights
properties.summary: Before dawn, a store owner in Highland and then police officers in Lebanon, Summerfield, Shiloh and Dupo independently reported a large, low triangular object with bright lights moving south-west toward Scott AFB and the Mississippi.
properties.explanation: The FAA suggested an advertising blimp; the officers’ descriptions of speed and size are hard to reconcile with that.

properties.title: Mexican Air Force FLIR — Campeche
properties.shape: 11 bright infrared lights
properties.summary: A Mexican Air Force surveillance aircraft hunting drug flights recorded 11 bright objects on its infrared camera at about 11,500 ft. The Defence Department released the tape on 12 May 2004.
properties.explanation: Most analysts identified the lights as gas flares on Cantarell offshore oil platforms seen over the horizon by the infrared camera.

properties.title: Tinley Park lights
properties.place: Tinley Park and Oak Forest, Illinois
properties.shape: Three to four red lights in a triangle
properties.summary: On the evening of August 21, 2004, hundreds of people in Chicago's south suburbs watched three large red lights in a triangle drift slowly and silently across the sky. Many filmed them. The lights returned on October 31, 2004 and on several nights in 2005 and 2006, and appeared on national television. They are a prominent "black triangle" style case with plenty of video.
properties.explanation: Commonly attributed to balloons or kites carrying lights or flares, which match the slow drift and the colour. No one has come forward, and the cause has not been confirmed.

properties.title: USS Nimitz "Tic Tac"
properties.place: Pacific Ocean ~100 mi SW of San Diego
properties.evidence: video, sensor-data, radar, pilot-witness, military-witness, official-document
properties.shape: White, smooth 40-ft "Tic Tac"
properties.summary: For days the cruiser USS Princeton’s SPY-1 radar tracked objects appearing at about 80,000 ft, dropping rapidly toward the sea and hovering. On 14 November, Cdr. David Fravor and Lt. Cdr. Alex Dietrich were vectored to a contact and saw a white Tic Tac-shaped object above a churning patch of ocean. It mirrored Fravor’s descent, then accelerated away; seconds later Princeton reported it at the pilots’ CAP point ~60 miles away. A later sortie filmed the FLIR1 video.
properties.explanation: The Pentagon released the FLIR1 video in 2020 and describes the object as unidentified. Skeptics argue the FLIR clip shows a distant aircraft; the pilots’ visual account is independent of the video.

properties.title: Río de la Plata — two airliners and a rising light
properties.place: Over the Río de la Plata between Ezeiza (Buenos Aires) and Carrasco (Montevideo)
properties.shape: A luminous object moving upwards
properties.summary: At about 4 a.m. on Monday, April 4, 2005, the pilot of a Uruguayan Aeromas cargo aircraft that had just left Ezeiza reported a luminous object near his aircraft over the Río de la Plata. The Ezeiza tower suggested it was an engine of a Lufthansa airliner in the area, but the Lufthansa pilot told him he had seen the light too, that it moved upwards and so could not be a meteorite, and called it a missile. A Uruguayan military pilot flying at the same time confirmed a fast luminous object. The reports went through the Carrasco and Ezeiza control towers; the Argentine Air Force recorded the report at Ezeiza, the Argentine armed forces said none of their aircraft or ships were in the area, and the Uruguayan Air Force opened an investigation. No result was published.

properties.title: Chicago O’Hare disc
properties.shape: Dark grey metallic disc, 6–24 ft
properties.summary: A ramp worker pushing back United Flight 446 saw a dark disc hovering low over Gate C-17; pilots, supervisors and mechanics came out to watch. Witnesses said it shot straight up through the overcast, leaving a clear hole in the clouds that closed moments later. The story emerged via a Chicago Tribune FOIA request.
properties.explanation: The FAA called it a "weather phenomenon" and did not investigate; conditions suited a hole-punch cloud. Nothing appeared on radar.

properties.title: Alderney airline sighting
properties.shape: Two bright yellow cigar/disc shapes with dark bands
properties.summary: Flying an Aurigny Trislander from Southampton to Alderney, Capt. Ray Bowyer saw two very large, brilliant yellow objects apparently stationary over the sea, confirmed by passengers and by the pilot of another aircraft. He filed an official report with the Civil Aviation Authority.
properties.explanation: Jersey radar showed only a faint primary return; proposed explanations include earthquake lights and sun dogs.

properties.title: Stephenville, Texas
properties.shape: Huge, silent, lit object up to a mile long
properties.summary: Dozens of people around Stephenville, including a private pilot and a local constable, reported a very large, silent object with bright lights followed by fighter jets. FOIA radar records later analysed by MUFON showed unidentified returns in the area.
properties.explanation: The Air Force said F-16s from the 457th Fighter Squadron were training in the area. A MUFON analysis of FAA radar data claimed an untransponded target heading toward the Crawford ranch; this is not officially confirmed.

properties.title: Cláudio — Military Police report
properties.shape: Luminous figures; lights in the sky
properties.summary: Over the night of November 19–20, 2008, officers of the Minas Gerais Military Police said they chased luminous humanoid figures and photographed lights in the sky around the town of Cláudio. Seven officers signed the report, which includes three photographs and a police incident record.

properties.title: Morristown lights (admitted hoax)
properties.shape: Five red lights in a line and arc
properties.summary: Around 8:15 p.m. on January 5, 2009, residents of Hanover Township, Morristown and nearby towns saw five red lights hanging in the sky and called 9-1-1. Tower staff at Morristown Airport also saw them, but radar showed nothing. TV news and UFO groups covered the lights, and they returned on four more nights. The two men who launched the balloons had also given TV interviews posing as witnesses. They called it a social experiment to show how unreliable eyewitness claims can be.
properties.explanation: Hoax. Joe Rudy and Chris Russo tied road flares to helium balloons and released them on five nights, then revealed it on April 1, 2009 with video of the launches. They were fined for disorderly conduct.

properties.title: Norwegian spiral
properties.place: Northern Norway and Sweden (seen from Troms and Finnmark)
properties.shape: Blue beam with an expanding white spiral
properties.summary: Before sunrise on December 9, 2009, people across northern Norway saw a blue-white light rise from behind the mountains, stop, and begin to spin. A glowing spiral grew outward and dissolved into a black hole-like disc. Photos and video went worldwide within hours. Astrophysicist Jonathan McDowell quickly suggested a failed Russian missile, and Moscow confirmed a Bulava test failure.
properties.explanation: A failed test of a Russian RSM-56 Bulava submarine-launched missile from the White Sea: the third stage malfunctioned, and the spinning missile sprayed fuel in a spiral lit by the Sun. The Russian Defence Ministry confirmed the failure the next day.

properties.title: Harbour Mille — the “missiles” over Fortune Bay
properties.shape: Three large grey or silver “bullets” with fire behind them and trails of smoke
properties.summary: At about sunset on Monday, January 25, 2010, Emmy Pardy and two friends in the small community of Harbour Mille, on Newfoundland’s south coast, saw three objects moving fast across the sky over Fortune Bay. Through binoculars Pardy described one as large and grey or silver with fire coming out of it; they trailed smoke. Darlene Stewart, who had been photographing the sunset, took pictures. When the photographs reached the news, the story became a small political puzzle: the RCMP first spoke of a missile launch and withdrew it, the Prime Minister’s Office said no rocket had been launched, the Defence Minister called the information “spotty”, and the French embassy said there had been no French military activity near Newfoundland or Saint-Pierre and Miquelon.
properties.explanation: Canada and France both said no missile or rocket had been launched; France’s M51 test from the submarine Le Terrible was on a different day and did not match the time or direction. A Royal Military College engineer judged the object subsonic and much smaller than a missile; federal officials suggested model rockets, which the witnesses rejected; and a television station later aired viewer video from the same time that showed a passing aircraft, whose contrail lit by the setting sun would look like a fiery trail. The RCMP closed the file as an unexplained sighting.

properties.title: The spiral over eastern Australia — Falcon 9’s first flight
properties.place: Eastern Australia: New South Wales, the Australian Capital Territory and Queensland
properties.shape: A large white light with a spiral, “lollipop-type swirl”
properties.summary: Before dawn on Saturday, June 5, 2010, people across New South Wales, the ACT and Queensland saw a large white light with a spiral around it, which seemed to hover briefly and then drift east out of sight. ABC News received dozens of photographs and videos. Astronomers first suggested space junk, a satellite or a rocket, and Sydney Observatory’s Geoffrey Wyatt suggested a rocket spun for stability. The answer came within a day: the Falcon 9 rocket, flying for the first time, had lifted off from Florida at 2:45 p.m. EDT on June 4 (4:45 a.m. in Sydney), and its second stage, with the Dragon qualification unit attached, was due over eastern Australia between about 5:30 and 5:45 a.m. The second stage had been rotating unexpectedly during the flight.
properties.explanation: The second stage of the first SpaceX Falcon 9, launched from Cape Canaveral at 18:45 UTC on June 4 with a test Dragon capsule, passed over eastern Australia about an hour later. The stage was rolling, and propellant or gas leaking from it formed a lit spiral, as the Bulava missile’s did over Norway six months earlier. Satellite observers matched the time and the ground track; Sydney Observatory also said it was the rocket.

properties.title: Hangzhou Xiaoshan Airport closure
properties.shape: Bright object over the airport
properties.summary: A bright unidentified object above the airport led authorities to close Xiaoshan and divert flights for about an hour.
properties.explanation: Chinese UFO research groups found no radar images and concluded the object was probably an aircraft, possibly military.

properties.title: Montevideo — the photo from the national team’s homecoming
properties.place: Palacio Legislativo and Avenida del Libertador, Montevideo
properties.shape: A semicircular object in the sky
properties.summary: On July 13, 2010, huge crowds met Uruguay’s football team at the Palacio Legislativo in Montevideo after its fourth place at the World Cup. One fan’s photograph, and others taken at the same spot, showed a semicircular object in the sky, and the picture spread as a UFO. The Uruguayan Air Force’s commission for UFO reports, CRIDOVNI, examined it and reported on July 28: it put the chance of fraud by the photographer or anyone else, and of a psychological effect, at zero, but gave a 97% probability to a conventional object, something like a piece of nylon, paper or cloth lifted by the rising air currents over Avenida del Libertador. No one who had seen the object itself came forward.
properties.explanation: The Uruguayan Air Force’s commission CRIDOVNI found the photographs genuine but rated a conventional cause 97% likely: a light object such as nylon, paper or cloth carried up by rising air over the avenue, with no one having seen anything at the time.

properties.title: El Bosque Air Base — the object in the air-show video
properties.shape: A small dark object darting past the jets
properties.summary: On the morning of November 5, 2010, the Chilean Air Force held a change-of-command ceremony with an air show at El Bosque Air Base in Santiago, with the Halcones aerobatic team, F-5s and F-16s. An engineer from the nearby aircraft factory, reviewing his own video in slow motion, noticed a small object that seemed to loop near the jets, and handed it to CEFAA, the committee of the civil aviation directorate that studies aerial phenomena. CEFAA gathered seven videos from different spectators and, at a press conference on March 13, 2012, said an astronomer had ruled out a meteoroid, space debris, a bird and an aircraft, estimated the object’s speed at over 6,500 km/h and said the incident could not be explained scientifically. Nobody at the show had noticed anything. Critics pointed out that the speed holds only if the object was far away; analyses of the original frames by the HoaxKiller project and others found the shape and motion of an insect a few metres from the lens.
properties.explanation: Chile’s aerial-phenomena committee CEFAA said the object could not be explained and estimated a speed of thousands of km/h, which depends entirely on an assumed distance. Independent analysts, among them the HoaxKiller project and the neurologist Steven Novella, showed that the frames match an insect flying close to the camera, which nobody present would have noticed.

properties.title: The “mystery missile” off Los Angeles — an airliner’s contrail
properties.place: Over the Pacific about 35 miles west of Los Angeles, north of Santa Catalina Island
properties.shape: A thick, glowing vapour trail apparently rising from the sea, with a bright head
properties.summary: At about 5:15 p.m. on November 8, 2010, a KCBS news helicopter filmed what looked like a missile climbing from the sea about 35 miles west of Los Angeles, a thick vapour trail glowing orange against the sunset with a bright point at its head. The footage ran on every network as the “mystery missile”, and for a day and a half nobody official could say what it was: the Pentagon said it was not a Defense Department launch, NORAD and Northern Command said it was no foreign military launch and no threat, the Navy said it was not theirs, and the FAA had approved no commercial launch. Contrail specialists and the analyst John Pike said at once that it was an aircraft contrail seen end-on, the head of the trail moving far too slowly for a rocket; the FAA’s radar replays found no fast unknown target, and on November 10 the Pentagon said there was “no evidence to suggest that this is anything else other than a condensation trail from an aircraft.” NASA researchers later found the trail on the GOES-11 weather-satellite image as a long horizontal streak. A few experts said they could not rule out a missile, but the incident is now a textbook example of foreshortened perspective.
properties.explanation: A condensation trail from an airliner flying towards the camera, which made a horizontal trail look like a vertical column lit by the setting sun. The FAA’s radar replays found no fast unidentified target, the Pentagon said there was no evidence it was anything else, and NASA’s contrail specialists found the trail on GOES-11 satellite imagery as a horizontal streak. US Airways Flight 808 from Honolulu and UPS Flight 902 were named as candidates.

properties.title: The light over the Dome of the Rock (hoax)
properties.place: Dome of the Rock, Temple Mount (Haram al-Sharif), Old City of Jerusalem
properties.shape: A bright white light that descends, hovers over the dome, flashes and shoots straight up
properties.summary: In late January 2011 a YouTube video appeared showing a small bright light dropping slowly toward the Dome of the Rock some time after midnight on January 28, hovering just above the golden dome, flashing, and then shooting straight up out of sight. A second clip from another angle followed, then two more, posted under the challenge “Have fun debunking this one”. The videos went round the world, with commentators noting that the multiple viewpoints made them hard to dismiss. Within days investigators pointed to the anonymous sources, the lack of any other witness in one of the most watched places on Earth, the missing reflection on the dome and signs of editing, and the case became a standard example of a digitally inserted UFO.
properties.explanation: The videos were faked. They were posted anonymously; nobody else among the many people in and around the Old City reported the light; it casts no reflection on the gilded dome; one clip was filmed off a monitor screen; and the analyst Robert Sheaffer showed that the camera shake had been added with an edge-mirroring “motion tile” effect. Nobody has owned up, but no one who examined the clips found them genuine.

properties.title: Santiago — the silver spheres over the Paseo Bulnes
properties.shape: Six bright silvery spheres
properties.summary: On Friday, May 11, 2012, hundreds of people in the centre of Santiago stopped to watch a group of six bright, silvery spheres in the sky. Photographs and videos spread under the hashtag #OvnisEnStgo, and the sighting became a national talking point within hours. The same day it emerged that the spheres were silver helium balloons released from the Paseo Bulnes by students of the Universidad Mayor’s school of architecture, as an installation in a competition between four student groups intended to screen the view towards the La Moneda palace.
properties.explanation: The objects were silver helium balloons released from the Paseo Bulnes by architecture students of the Universidad Mayor, one of four groups in a school competition; the installation was meant to block the view of La Moneda.

properties.title: Ladakh lights — the “Chinese drones” that were planets
properties.place: Thakung post, near Pangong Tso, eastern Ladakh, India
properties.shape: Yellowish luminous spheres rising from the horizon on the Chinese side
properties.summary: From August 2012, soldiers and border police on the Line of Actual Control in eastern Ladakh reported luminous objects rising over the Chinese side and staying up for hours. With Chinese drones a real concern, the army logged 329 sightings by February 2013 and counted 155 apparent violations of the border. At the army’s request, two astronomers from the Indian Institute of Astrophysics in Bengaluru travelled to Thakung, near Pangong Tso, and measured the objects with a theodolite: one was visible from about 6 p.m. to 5 a.m., the other from about 4 a.m., and they moved with the stars. They were Jupiter and Venus. A soldier’s note that one object rose about four minutes earlier every day, as a planet does, had already pointed the same way.
properties.explanation: Astronomers of the Indian Institute of Astrophysics, sent at the army’s request, identified the two brightest “objects” as Jupiter and Venus, made unusually bright by the altitude; their apparent motion was the sky turning. The defence minister told Parliament there was no conclusive proof of UFOs.

properties.title: Chelyabinsk meteor — and the “UFO that shot it down”
properties.place: Chelyabinsk Oblast, Russia; the air burst south of Chelyabinsk
properties.shape: A fireball brighter than the Sun, leaving a long, twisted smoke trail
properties.summary: At 9:20 a.m. on February 15, 2013, a fireball brighter than the Sun crossed the morning sky of the southern Urals from the east and exploded south of Chelyabinsk, leaving a smoke trail tens of kilometres long. A minute or more later the shock wave blew in windows across the city: 1,491 people sought medical help, most cut by glass, and more than 7,000 buildings were damaged. Because Russian drivers routinely run dashboard cameras, the event was filmed from hundreds of angles, which let scientists reconstruct its path and orbit within days. Within hours, too, clips circulated claiming that a small object had flown into the meteor and shattered it, and the UFO commentator Gennady Belimov said a UFO had shot it down; a survey by the newspaper Noviye Izvestia found barely half its readers accepted the official account. The fragments in museum collections are ordinary chondrite.
properties.explanation: A near-Earth asteroid about 20 m across entered at about 19 km/s at a shallow angle and exploded some 30 km up with the energy of roughly 400–500 kilotons of TNT, recorded by infrasound stations worldwide and by U.S. government sensors. Meteorites were collected across the strewn field, and a 654 kg fragment was raised from Lake Chebarkul in October 2013. Claims that videos showed a UFO destroying the meteor, and a newspaper survey in which many readers preferred a weapon test or a crashing alien ship, rest on nothing but the footage of the meteor itself.

properties.title: Chelyabinsk meteor — and the “UFO that shot it down”
properties.label: Meteor entry (approximate)

properties.title: Collahuasi mine — CEFAA’s “UFO” photographs
properties.place: Collahuasi copper mine, 4,300 m up in the Tarapacá Andes
properties.shape: A silver disc, estimated 5 to 10 m across
properties.summary: On a clear day in mid-April 2013, four technicians at the Collahuasi copper mine, high in the Andes of northern Chile, watched a silver disc hover silently for more than an hour at what they estimated as about 600 m, and one of them took photographs with a compact camera. They kept quiet until the mine’s chief engineer sent two pictures to CEFAA in February 2014. A CEFAA analyst at the meteorological office ruled out lenticular cloud, aircraft, drones, balloons and birds, found the object brighter than reflected sunlight would make it, and concluded it “can be qualified as a UFO”; the director, retired General Ricardo Bermúdez, released the study in July 2014 but said it was one analyst’s view and that the committee had to be cautious. The witnesses never answered CEFAA’s requests to talk, the originals and the order of the pictures were uncertain, and critics noted that a disc against blue sky gives no way to judge its size or distance. CEFAA filed the case as unexplained.

properties.title: Aguadilla thermal video (DHS)
properties.place: Rafael Hernández Airport, Aguadilla, Puerto Rico
properties.shape: Small hot object; appears to enter and exit the sea
properties.summary: A Customs and Border Protection DHC-8 recorded a small, hot object crossing the airport and heading out over the ocean, where it appeared to plunge into the water and re-emerge. The leaked video became a staple of UAP analysis; AARO published a 3D reconstruction video in 2025.
properties.explanation: AARO assesses with high confidence the objects showed no anomalous speed or behaviour: a reconstruction of the sensor’s look angle shows two objects travelling near each other in a straight line at wind speed, never entering the water. Its case resolution assesses with moderate confidence that they were a pair of sky lanterns. Some independent analysts still dispute this.

properties.title: Aguadilla thermal video (DHS)
properties.label: Objects (approximate path; AARO: moving at wind speed)

properties.title: Naga fireballs of the Mekong
properties.place: The Mekong around Phon Phisai and Nong Khai, Thailand, and the Lao bank opposite
properties.shape: Reddish-pink balls of light rising silently from the river to a few hundred metres
properties.summary: Every year on the night of Wan Ok Phansa, the full moon that ends the Buddhist Rains Retreat in October, crowds gather along a 250 km stretch of the Mekong centred on Phon Phisai to watch glowing reddish balls rise silently from the water, climb a few hundred metres and vanish. Local belief credits the phaya nak, the serpent said to live in the river; until the mid-1980s they were called ghost lights, and the Phayanak festival now draws tens of thousands of visitors. The photograph here was taken near Nong Khai on Ok Phansa night, 2013. Sceptics point to gunfire and flares from the Lao bank, which the crowds would not hear across the river; believers point out that the lights also appear over ponds and smaller rivers away from the border.
properties.explanation: In 2002 a documentary on Thailand’s iTV filmed Lao soldiers on the far bank firing tracer rounds into the air during the festival, and the Thai biologist Jessada Denduangboripant, after studying footage, concluded the lights were flares fired from the other side. Neither explanation is accepted locally, and a Lao government inquiry in 2021, held during a COVID-19 curfew with police on the river, said it was “extremely unlikely” anyone could have fired unnoticed. The idea of phosphine or methane from the riverbed has no scientific support.

properties.title: Chilean Navy helicopter FLIR video
properties.place: Coast between San Antonio and Quinteros, Chile
properties.shape: Flat, elongated object with two hot discharges
properties.summary: On November 11, 2014 a Chilean Navy helicopter on coastal patrol west of Santiago, at about 4,500 feet, picked up an unknown object on its high-definition infrared camera. The two-man crew also saw it with the naked eye for more than ten minutes. The captain described a flat, elongated object with two thermal discharges that did not line up with its direction of travel, and the video shows what looks like a chemical plume. The Navy’s aerial-phenomena office CEFAA examined it and later released the footage, saying it could not be sure what it was. Sceptics later said the images match the contrail of a distant aircraft.
properties.explanation: Chile’s aerial-phenomena office (CEFAA) left the case open because it could not be certain of the object’s nature. Later analyses by sceptics proposed an aircraft’s contrail and exhaust seen by infrared as the likely cause.

properties.title: USS Theodore Roosevelt — Gimbal & GoFast
properties.place: Atlantic warning areas off Jacksonville, Florida
properties.evidence: video, sensor-data, radar, pilot-witness, military-witness, official-document
properties.shape: Rotating lozenge (Gimbal); small fast object (GoFast)
properties.summary: In 2014–2015 F/A-18F crews of the Roosevelt strike group reported frequent unknown objects on their upgraded APG-79 radars off the East Coast. Two ATFLIR clips — "Gimbal", with a crew member exclaiming about "a whole fleet of them", and "GoFast", a small object skimming over the ocean — were released by the Pentagon in April 2020.
properties.explanation: Both videos were officially released and remain "unidentified" per DoD. Analysts such as Mick West argue GoFast shows a slow object (e.g. a balloon) at ~13,000 ft that only looks fast and low because of parallax, and that Gimbal’s rotation is a glare artifact of the ATFLIR pod. AARO later published a case resolution for GoFast worked out from the sensor’s geometry and the winds aloft.

properties.title: The light over California — a Trident II test from USS Kentucky
properties.place: The Navy’s Pacific Test Range off Southern California; seen from California, Nevada and Arizona
properties.shape: A bright light trailing a glowing, expanding cone of blue-white vapour
properties.summary: Shortly after 6 p.m. on Saturday, November 7, 2015, a bright light rose over the Pacific west of Los Angeles and grew into a glowing, spreading cone of vapour that was seen from the Bay Area to San Diego and as far as Nevada and Arizona. Police and sheriff’s offices across Southern California were flooded with calls, and the videos spread across social media as a UFO, a meteor or a missile gone wrong. The Navy said that evening that its Strategic Systems Programs had carried out a scheduled test flight of an unarmed Trident II D5 missile from USS Kentucky in the Pacific Test Range; such launches are not announced in advance. The effect, sunlight catching the exhaust plume high above a darkened ground, is the same as the Iridium launch of 2017 and many Vandenberg twilight launches before it.
properties.explanation: An unarmed Trident II (D5) ballistic missile fired by the submarine USS Kentucky during a scheduled test in the Pacific Test Range. The Navy confirmed it the same evening; its exhaust plume, lit by sunlight high above the darkened ground, produced the expanding “twilight phenomenon”.

properties.title: Fireball over the West — a Chinese rocket stage re-entering
properties.shape: A slow procession of bright fragments with glowing trails
properties.summary: At about 9:36 p.m. on July 27, 2016, a slow procession of bright fragments with long trails crossed the sky over California, Nevada and Utah, seen from Los Angeles to Las Vegas and Salt Lake City and filmed by many people. It moved far more slowly than a meteor. Within hours the Joint Space Operations Center at Vandenberg confirmed that it had tracked the re-entry of the spent second stage of China’s new Long March 7 rocket, launched a month earlier, and later removed the object from the satellite catalogue as decayed. The astronomer Jonathan McDowell identified the stage from the tracking data. Like the Zond IV fragments of 1968, it is the kind of event that turns into a “formation of craft” in some witnesses’ descriptions.
properties.explanation: The Joint Space Operations Center confirmed that the objects were the second stage of China’s Long March 7 rocket, launched on its first flight on June 25, 2016, re-entering the atmosphere and breaking up.

properties.title: Fireball over the West — a Chinese rocket stage re-entering
properties.label: Long March 7 second stage re-entering (approximate)

properties.title: Jeffreys Bay — a cargo crew’s green light
properties.place: About 10 nautical miles off Jeffreys Bay, Eastern Cape
properties.shape: A glowing green object
properties.summary: At about 9:30 p.m. on December 12, 2016, the crew of a Boeing 737 cargo flight from Cape Town to Port Elizabeth, about 10 nautical miles off the coast at Jeffreys Bay, saw a glowing green object climb past the cockpit to the cloud layer some 1,000 feet above them, then turn and drop back past them toward the sea at high speed. Port Elizabeth air traffic control, fearing a vessel or aircraft in distress had fired a flare, asked the National Sea Rescue Institute to check; its Jeffreys Bay station watched overnight. The object was not seen again and no craft was overdue.
properties.explanation: A green parachute flare was suspected first and ruled out because a flare cannot climb that high; the NSRI found no vessel or aircraft overdue or missing. Green is the usual colour of a bright meteor, but a meteor does not climb, which is what the crew described. The NSRI called the incident “a mystery”.

properties.title: AARO’s “Southeast Asia Triangles” — fishing nets
properties.place: A river in Southeast Asia (exact location withheld)
properties.shape: Six dark triangles in a line
properties.summary: A commercial satellite image taken at 07:35 UTC on August 30, 2017 showed six dark triangles in a staggered line, and an intelligence analyst flagged them as possibly anomalous and a risk to navigation. AARO reviewed the case in 2023. Its partners found a clearer image of the same place from February 2017 that showed the triangles as cone-shaped fishing nets anchored in a river, all about 11 by 7 metres; later images from late 2022 and early 2023 showed the same shapes with turbidity trailing downstream, proving they were in the water, and stock footage showed such nets on that river. AARO closed the case as fishing nets. Its report names only “Southeast Asia”; the image’s time stamps, 07:35Z and 14:05 local, match Myanmar’s clock (UTC+6:30), and the marker is placed there only approximately.
properties.explanation: AARO, with intelligence and three science-and-technology partners, found “almost certainly” static, cone-shaped fishing nets on a river, each about 11 by 7 m, matched in other satellite images from 2017, 2022 and 2023 and in stock footage of the same river.

properties.title: The Los Angeles “UFO” — SpaceX Iridium-4 launch
properties.place: Vandenberg Air Force Base; seen across Southern California and as far as Arizona
properties.shape: A glowing, expanding jellyfish-like cloud with a bright point at its head
properties.summary: At 5:27 p.m. on December 22, 2017, twenty minutes after sunset, a Falcon 9 lifted off from Space Launch Complex 4E at Vandenberg carrying ten Iridium NEXT satellites. High above the darkening ground the exhaust was still in sunlight, and the expanding plume, the staging and the fairing separation drew a luminous, jellyfish-like cloud seen from Los Angeles to Las Vegas and Phoenix. Phones and social media filled with pictures of a UFO; the Los Angeles Fire Department put out an advisory that the “mysterious light in the sky” was the launch, and Elon Musk posted the video as a “nuclear alien UFO from North Korea”. The launch had been announced in advance; twilight launches from Vandenberg have caused the same reports since.
properties.explanation: A scheduled Falcon 9 launch carrying ten Iridium NEXT satellites from Vandenberg; the exhaust plume, lit by the Sun after sunset on the ground, made the glowing cloud. The Los Angeles Fire Department issued an advisory that the light came from the launch.

properties.title: The Los Angeles “UFO” — SpaceX Iridium-4 launch
properties.label: Falcon 9 ascent (approximate)

properties.title: Learjet and American 1095 over Arizona — “something just passed over us”
properties.place: Over southern Arizona, east of the Sonoran Desert National Monument
properties.shape: A bright, reflective object several thousand feet above the airliners
properties.summary: On the afternoon of February 24, 2018, a Learjet 36 flying east at about 37,000 ft over southern Arizona asked Albuquerque Center whether anything had just passed over it; the controller had nothing, and the pilot said something had. The controller asked American Airlines Flight 1095, an Airbus A321 following on the same route, to watch for traffic above it within the next 15 miles; a few minutes later its crew reported that something had passed over them, two or three thousand feet higher, going the other way, and, asked whether it was moving or hovering, said it was very bright or reflective. Someone on the frequency suggested a Google balloon, which the airline crew doubted, and someone else called it a UFO. The FAA released the recording to reporters in March; it said the controller could not see any other aircraft and suggested a high-altitude balloon. Nothing more was published.
properties.explanation: An FAA spokesperson suggested a high-altitude balloon, which need not carry a transponder or tell air traffic control; the area sees regular research and weather balloons. The controller could not see anything on radar, and the pilots, who saw it pass above and in the opposite direction, did not sound convinced. No report of a military aircraft or drone in the area emerged.

properties.title: Ireland — airline pilots report fast lights
properties.shape: Very bright lights moving at high speed
properties.summary: At about 6:47 on the morning of November 9, 2018 the pilot of a British Airways flight from Montreal to London radioed Shannon air traffic control to ask whether military exercises were under way. A “very bright light” had come up on the left of the aircraft and “rapidly veered to the north”, then disappeared at very high speed. The crew of a Virgin Atlantic flight reported two bright lights that banked to the right and climbed away at what the pilot called “astronomical” speed, “like Mach 2”. Controllers saw nothing on radar, and no military exercises were taking place. The Irish Aviation Authority said it would investigate by confidentially interviewing the pilots. More than one crew reported it, and the story was carried by news outlets around the world.
properties.explanation: One pilot suggested a meteor or an object in re-entry, and an astronomer at the Armagh Observatory said the lights were most likely meteors. Air traffic control saw nothing on radar and no military exercises were running, so nothing has been confirmed.

properties.title: USS Omaha sphere & USS Russell "pyramids"
properties.shape: Spherical object descending into the sea; flashing pyramid shapes
properties.summary: During July 2019, several Navy ships off Southern California reported drone-like objects around them at night. A CIC video from USS Omaha shows a sphere flying over the ocean and apparently descending into the water; night-vision footage from USS Russell shows blinking pyramid-shaped lights. Both leaked in 2021 and were confirmed as authentic Navy footage.
properties.explanation: The Pentagon confirmed the leaked clips were taken by Navy personnel. Analysts attribute the "pyramids" to the triangular aperture of a night-vision lens (bokeh) on aircraft/stars, and the Omaha sphere to a distant aircraft or balloon.

properties.title: Colorado and Nebraska drone swarms
properties.place: Phillips County and the plains of north-eastern Colorado
properties.shape: Drones with a wingspan of about 6 ft and blinking lights, in groups of six to ten, flying grid patterns
properties.summary: In December 2019, residents and deputies in north-eastern Colorado and western Nebraska began reporting drones with wingspans of about six feet flying in groups of six to ten, at 200 to 500 feet, in grid patterns across the plains, mostly between about 7 and 10 p.m.; one witness counted 19. County sheriffs asked the public for information, and more than 70 local, state and federal agencies met in Brush on January 6, 2020. The FAA said no drone company or test site had authorized flights there, and the Air Force, which had run counter-drone exercises at F. E. Warren AFB, would neither claim nor deny the drones. As the sightings spread, more and more turned out to be planets, stars and airliners, and the state ended its search later that month.
properties.explanation: State and federal agencies found that most reports were planets, stars, aircraft and hobby drones, and the Colorado Department of Public Safety stood its effort down in January 2020. The large, grid-flying drones of the first reports were never tied to an operator.

properties.title: Sendai’s white balloon
properties.shape: A large white sphere with crossed struts and propellers hanging beneath
properties.summary: On the morning of June 17, 2020, residents of northern Sendai began posting photographs of a large white sphere hanging almost motionless in the sky, with crossed struts and propellers beneath it. The Sendai office of the Japan Meteorological Agency said it looked like a weather balloon “but it’s not ours”, police sent a helicopter but could not identify it, Kyushu University denied it was theirs, and the government said only that it was aware of the object, which later drifted out over the Pacific. In February 2023, after the Chinese balloon crossed the United States, Japan’s Ministry of Defense re-examined the Sendai balloon and similar ones over Kagoshima in 2019 and Aomori in 2021, and concluded that they were strongly presumed to be Chinese unmanned reconnaissance balloons. It protested to Beijing, which said Japan had no proof.
properties.explanation: A balloon. On February 14, 2023, after the Chinese balloon was shot down over the United States, Japan’s Ministry of Defense said that the balloons seen over its territory in November 2019, June 2020 and September 2021 were “strongly presumed” to be unmanned reconnaissance balloons flown by China; China rejected the claim.

properties.title: American Airlines 2292 — “cruise-missile type of thing”
properties.place: Northeastern New Mexico, at about 36,000 ft
properties.shape: Long cylinder, “almost like a cruise missile”
properties.summary: On February 21, 2021, at about 12:29 p.m. local time, the crew of American Airlines Flight 2292, an Airbus A320 flying from Cincinnati to Phoenix at about 36,000 feet over the north-east corner of New Mexico, radioed: “Do you have any targets up here? We just had something go right over the top of us. I hate to say this, but it looked like a long cylindrical object that almost looked like a cruise missile type of thing, moving really fast right over the top of us.” The transmission was recorded by Steve Douglass, a radio listener. American Airlines at first denied that it was authentic, then confirmed that it was from Flight 2292 after talking to the crew. The FAA said controllers saw nothing on radar, and the Pentagon said it had no tests in the area.
properties.explanation: No explanation has been given. The FAA said air traffic controllers saw no object on their radar. The Pentagon said the military was not conducting tests in the area that day, and the FBI said it was aware of the report.

properties.title: Lights over Seattle and Portland — a Falcon 9 stage re-entering
properties.place: Over western Oregon and Washington; debris in Grant County, Washington
properties.shape: A cluster of bright fragments with glowing trails, moving slowly across the sky
properties.summary: At about 9 p.m. on March 25, 2021, people from Portland to Seattle saw a slow cluster of bright lights with trails cross the sky, breaking apart as it went, and posted videos of what many took for a meteor shower or a formation of craft. The National Weather Service office in Seattle said that night that the lights were the remnants of a Falcon 9 second stage re-entering; the astronomer Jonathan McDowell confirmed that the stage, left in orbit after a Starlink launch on March 4 when its de-orbit burn failed, had come down at about 04:00 UTC on March 26. Days later a farmer in Grant County, in central Washington, reported to the sheriff an object that had left a four-inch dent in his field: a composite-overwrapped pressure vessel from the stage, which SpaceX identified and collected. It is one of the few re-entries where the identification, the tracking and a piece of the object all came together.
properties.explanation: The second stage of a SpaceX Falcon 9 that launched Starlink satellites on March 4, 2021, failed to make its de-orbit burn and re-entered uncontrolled about three weeks later. The National Weather Service in Seattle identified the lights the same night, and a pressure vessel from the stage was found on a farm in Grant County, Washington, and recovered by SpaceX.

properties.title: Lights over Seattle and Portland — a Falcon 9 stage re-entering
properties.label: Falcon 9 second stage re-entering (approximate)

properties.title: Three objects on a Western U.S. military range
properties.shape: Three small dots on infrared
properties.summary: Shown by AARO at NASA’s UAP Independent Study Team public meeting (May 31, 2023) as an example of a resolved case: three unidentified infrared dots turned out to be three separate commercial aircraft at great distance.
properties.explanation: AARO matched the three dots to commercial airliners far from the infrared sensor using flight and radar data.

properties.title: Maldonado — the UFO videos that were a festival campaign
properties.place: Parque del Jagüel, Punta del Este, Maldonado
properties.shape: Not described; staged footage
properties.summary: On August 12, 2021, videos circulated in Uruguay that appeared to show a UFO landing, U.S. aircraft and U.S. scientists at the Parque del Jagüel in Maldonado, with one clip presented as a breaking-news report by a well-known Subrayado journalist. The Uruguayan Air Force’s commission for UFO reports, CRIDOVNI, examined the material and announced the next day that, having investigated the evidence and analysed the possible events, they “are not real”. The clips turned out to be part of a promotional campaign for the America Rockstars music festival.
properties.explanation: The Uruguayan Air Force’s CRIDOVNI investigated and said the events “are not real”: the videos were part of a promotional campaign for the America Rockstars festival, including a staged television news flash.

properties.title: AC-130J “cold orbs” over the Gulf of Oman
properties.shape: “Cold orbs”, approximately four feet in diameter
properties.summary: On September 8, 2021, the crew of a U.S. Special Operations AC-130J Ghostrider gunship over the Gulf of Oman tracked what an Intelligence Information Report (DOW-UAP-D101) calls “cold orbs” about four feet in diameter. U.S. Central Command sent AARO six short videos, recorded at the same time on a mobile phone pointed at the infrared sensor display. In most of them a small area of contrast stays in the centre of the sensor’s view; in two overlapping clips a larger and a smaller one cross the frame and come back. The Department of War released them as DOW-UAP-PR117 to PR122 in 2026, without a determination.
properties.explanation: AARO released the six clips in 2026 as unresolved. They are phone recordings of the gunship’s infrared display, not the sensor data itself, which limits what can be measured; the accompanying Intelligence Information Report describes “cold orbs” about four feet across.

properties.title: FBI files — orbs over one place in the north-eastern U.S.
properties.place: A sparsely populated place in the north-eastern United States (withheld)
properties.shape: Bright lights splitting into several rotating points; red spheres; a “plasma-like” sphere over a pond; two red orbs moving together
properties.summary: Among the files the FBI released through the Department of War in 2026 are four phone videos from the same sparsely populated area of the north-eastern United States. In November 2021, at about 5 a.m., an eyewitness filmed a bright light near the horizon that resolved into several lights rotating erratically around each other. In March 2022 the same witness filmed two red lights, the lower turning slowly around the upper; in October 2024, a luminous “plasma-like” sphere that hung over a pond for about 45 minutes, shedding smaller points. In July 2025 a couple within 25 miles of those places saw a red sphere hovering 25 feet above their backyard, then a second above it; the two moved off together, silently, over the trees. The FBI calls the first witness highly credible and says the government authenticated the 2024 video; it does not say what the lights were.
properties.explanation: Released in 2026 with the witnesses’ statements and the FBI’s view that they are credible, but with no determination of what the lights were. The phone videos are short, shaky and distant.

properties.title: The Navy’s night-vision image shown to Congress — drones
properties.place: Naval exercise areas off the U.S. East Coast (exact place and date withheld)
properties.shape: Points of light in a night-vision image
properties.summary: At the House Intelligence subcommittee’s open hearing on unidentified aerial phenomena on May 17, 2022, the first public congressional hearing on the subject in more than fifty years, the Deputy Director of Naval Intelligence, Scott Bray, showed an image taken through night-vision goggles with a single-lens reflex camera during Navy exercises off the East Coast in early 2022. Bray told the committee that, using information from other sightings, the Navy had reclassified the objects as unmanned aerial systems. He also showed an unresolved clip of a small sphere flashing past a Navy fighter’s cockpit. The image is in the Pentagon’s official release on DVIDS.
properties.explanation: The Navy said the objects were later reclassified as unmanned aerial systems, on the strength of other data and similar sightings.

properties.title: The blue spiral over New Zealand — a Falcon 9 upper stage
properties.place: Across New Zealand, photographed from Queenstown, Stewart Island and Motueka
properties.shape: A glowing blue-white spiral, growing as it moved across the sky
properties.summary: At about 7:27 p.m. on Sunday, June 19, 2022, people across New Zealand saw a bright spiral of light appear and grow as it moved across the night sky. Alasdair Burns, a tour operator on Stewart Island, was alerted by text and photographed it; Clare Rehill photographed it above Queenstown, and an observer in Motueka posted that it was “just happening”. Photographs went round the world the next day. Astronomers quickly tied it to a Falcon 9 launched three hours earlier, whose second stage was passing over New Zealand while it vented fuel before its de-orbit burn.
properties.explanation: The upper stage of the SpaceX Falcon 9 that launched the Globalstar FM15 satellite from Cape Canaveral at 04:27 UTC that day, venting its leftover propellant before the burn that brought it down into the Pacific. The New Plymouth Astronomical Society and satellite observers matched the time; the same kind of spiral has followed other Falcon 9 launches.

properties.title: MQ-9 "Middle East orb"
properties.shape: Silver, orb-like object
properties.summary: Shown by AARO director Sean Kirkpatrick at the April 19, 2023 Senate Armed Services hearing: an MQ-9 Reaper’s sensor briefly tracks a silver orb crossing its field of view — typical of the many reports AARO receives with minimal data.
properties.explanation: AARO: the object did not show anomalous behaviour but remains unidentified for lack of data.

properties.title: Long March 5B core stage burns up over Sarawak
properties.place: Over Sarawak, Malaysia, toward the Sulu Sea
properties.shape: A line of bright fragments, like a slow meteor shower
properties.summary: Just before 1 a.m. on July 31, 2022, people in Kuching and elsewhere in Sarawak saw a slow procession of bright fragments cross the sky, which many took at first for a meteor shower, and filmed it on their phones. It was the core stage of the Long March 5B that had launched China’s Wentian laboratory module a week earlier. Unlike most rocket stages it had reached orbit, and its fall had been tracked and debated for days because China had not released trajectory details. The Malaysian Space Agency said the debris had crossed Malaysian airspace and fallen into the Sulu Sea; pieces were reported in Sarawak and West Kalimantan.
properties.explanation: The 21-tonne core stage of the Chinese Long March 5B rocket that launched the Wentian space-station module on July 24, 2022, falling back uncontrolled. The Malaysian Space Agency confirmed that its burning debris crossed Malaysian airspace, and the re-entry point was given as 9.1° N, 119.0° E, in the Sulu Sea.

properties.title: Long March 5B core stage burns up over Sarawak
properties.label: Core stage re-entering (approximate)

properties.title: Porto Alegre — airline pilots report blinking lights
properties.place: Approach to Salgado Filho airport, Porto Alegre, Rio Grande do Sul
properties.shape: Lights switching on and off, one to three at a time, apparently stationary and higher than the aircraft
properties.summary: On the nights of November 4 and 5, 2022, crews approaching Porto Alegre reported lights in the sky to the controllers, and their radio exchanges were widely shared. The pilot of LATAM flight 3406 from São Paulo asked whether anyone had reported objects over the city and described lights that switched on and off, sometimes one and sometimes two or three; the pilot of Azul 4657 from Belo Horizonte said he had seen them since leaving Minas Gerais and that they were well above his 38,000 ft. The tower said it could see them too, apparently stationary, and that they would not affect approaches; similar reports came from over Santa Catarina in late October and from four aircraft on November 8. The Air Force said its radars detected no unknown object. Astronomers suggested Starlink satellites catching the sun, searchlights on cloud and, for some videos, meteors; none was confirmed for the pilots’ sightings.
properties.explanation: Astronomers proposed several ordinary causes: sunlight flashing off Starlink satellites (an analysis of a video from Torres pointed to Starlink “almost 100%”), searchlights reflected by cloud, and meteors in other recordings. The Brazilian Air Force said its radars detected nothing unknown, and no single cause was confirmed for the pilots’ reports.

properties.title: MQ-9 records object with "wake" — South Asia
properties.shape: Object with apparent atmospheric wake
properties.summary: An MQ-9 filming another MQ-9 caught an object with an apparent wake crossing the frame. AARO showed it at the April 2023 Senate hearing and released both clips.
properties.explanation: AARO resolved the case in February 2024 (“Atmospheric Wakes”): frame-by-frame analysis and flight data showed a commuter aircraft flying near the two MQ-9s, and the apparent wake was the heat signature from its engines.

properties.title: AARO’s “Eglin UAP” — a lighting balloon
properties.place: Eglin Air Force Base training range, over the Gulf off north-west Florida
properties.shape: About 12 ft across: a rounded grey lower half and a cone on top, like an Apollo capsule
properties.summary: On January 26, 2023, a military pilot training over the Eglin range off Florida saw four objects on radar at 16,000 to 18,000 ft, apparently in formation. Only one was seen: about 12 ft across, grey and paneled, rounded below and cone-shaped above “like the Apollo spacecraft”, with an orange-red patch at its centre and “blurry air” beneath; the pilot later thought a vertical engine was attached to its side. The aircraft’s video recorder was out of service, so the infrared and visual sensor took two still images. When the jet closed to within 4,000 ft its radar failed, and the object sank into the clouds. AARO found that the circuit breaker had tripped on the same aircraft three times before, that the images matched a commercial lighting balloon with black and white halves, which it tested, and that the object moved with the wind at that height. It closed the case in October 2023 as very likely a balloon.
properties.explanation: AARO assessed with moderate confidence that it was a lighter-than-air object, such as a large commercial lighting balloon, a weather balloon or a large Mylar balloon, drifting with the wind; its intelligence and science-and-technology partners independently reached the same conclusion with high confidence. The radar failure was a circuit breaker that had tripped three times before.

properties.title: Chinese surveillance balloon
properties.shape: Large white balloon with solar-array payload
properties.summary: A high-altitude balloon from China crossed into U.S. airspace north of the Aleutians, drifted over Canada, passed over Malmstrom AFB in Montana and across the continent before being shot down off South Carolina. The event prompted NORAD to re-tune its radars, which led to the February 10–12 shoot-downs of three smaller unidentified objects.
properties.explanation: A PRC high-altitude surveillance balloon; shot down by an F-22 AIM-9X off Surfside Beach, South Carolina, and recovered by the U.S. Navy.

properties.title: The balloon over Colombia — China’s second airship
properties.place: Northern Colombian airspace; also reported over Costa Rica and on towards Venezuela
properties.shape: An object with the characteristics of a balloon
properties.summary: On the morning of Friday, February 3, 2023, the day the first Chinese balloon was crossing the United States, Colombia’s air-defence system detected an object “with characteristics similar to those of a balloon” in the north of the country at about 55,000 ft, moving at an average of 25 knots. The Colombian Air Force followed it until it left national airspace, said it posed no threat to national security or to aviation, and began working with other countries to establish its origin. Costa Rica also reported a balloon. The Pentagon said the same day that another suspected Chinese balloon was over Latin America, and later that these balloons were part of a fleet built for surveillance. On February 6 China confirmed the balloon was its own, calling it a civilian airship that, affected by the weather and with limited self-steering, had drifted into Latin American and Caribbean airspace.
properties.explanation: The Pentagon identified it as a second Chinese surveillance balloon; China said it was a civilian airship for flight tests that had strayed far off course because of the weather and its limited steering.

properties.title: February 2023 shoot-downs (Alaska, Yukon, Lake Huron)
properties.shape: Small octagonal / cylindrical objects at 20,000–40,000 ft
properties.summary: After re-tuning radars following the Chinese balloon, NORAD detected and shot down three small objects in three days: off Deadhorse, Alaska (Feb 10), over central Yukon (Feb 11) and over Lake Huron (Feb 12). The first AIM-9X fired at the Lake Huron object missed. Debris was never recovered.
properties.explanation: The White House said the three objects were most likely benign commercial or research balloons; none was recovered. An infrared video of the Lake Huron shoot-down was released in 2026 as DOW-UAP-PR071.

properties.title: Las Vegas backyard “landing”
properties.shape: A green flash streaking low across the sky; the family described tall beings with big eyes
properties.summary: At about 11:50 p.m. on April 30, 2023, a Las Vegas Metropolitan Police officer’s body camera caught a bright light streaking low across the night sky, and people across Nevada, eastern California, Arizona and Utah reported a green fireball to the American Meteor Society. About 40 minutes later a man called 911 to say that something had fallen into his backyard in the north-west of the valley and that there were two tall beings “100 percent not human” in it. Officers came, found nothing and closed the call as unfounded; the release of the bodycam footage in June made the story famous, and later drone footage of a circular mark in the dirt was offered as evidence. NASA’s planetary defense office said the light was “certainly” a meteor, less than a metre across.
properties.explanation: The flash was a bright meteor, according to NASA’s planetary defense office and reports to the American Meteor Society from four states. Nothing supports the “beings”: the police found nothing and closed the call as unfounded.

properties.title: Espora naval air base — the “battle” that the Navy denied
properties.place: Base Aeronaval Comandante Espora, Bahía Blanca, Buenos Aires province
properties.shape: Claimed: four black triangles
properties.summary: After 9 p.m. on September 5, 2023, residents near the Comandante Espora naval air base outside Bahía Blanca posted videos and called 911 about what they took for gunfire and explosions from the base, with a helicopter overhead. A private group, CEFORA, then claimed that four black triangular objects had flown over and landed at parts of the base, that personnel had fired on them, and that a laser from one had injured two or three soldiers; the story spread with memes across Argentina. Official sources at the base said the videos and audio were edited and that “the noises and images do not correspond to the place”, that there had been no exercise or shooting and nobody had seen anything, and that a helicopter had flown a scheduled routine patrol on its usual route. The police confirmed the calls, but no injury, damage or other record of an engagement ever appeared.
properties.explanation: Base sources said the circulating videos and audio were edited and did not come from the base, that no exercise or shooting took place and that staff saw nothing; the only activity was a helicopter on a scheduled routine patrol. The claims of triangular craft and a laser that wounded soldiers came from a private UFO group and were never supported by any record.

properties.title: The “Nazca mummies” shown to Mexico’s Congress
properties.place: Chamber of Deputies, San Lázaro, Mexico City (the figures came from the Nazca area of Peru)
properties.shape: Small three-fingered humanoid bodies
properties.summary: On September 12, 2023, at a hearing on unidentified phenomena in Mexico’s Chamber of Deputies, the journalist and UFO promoter Jaime Maussan unveiled two small, three-fingered bodies in glass cases, said they came from the Nazca region of Peru, were over 700 years old and were “non-human beings”, and cited studies at the National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM), whose scientists denied that the university had endorsed any such conclusion. Mexico’s Congress took no position. Maussan had promoted similar bodies from Peru in 2017, which Peruvian officials then called recently manufactured dolls. In October 2023 Peruvian customs seized two more figures bound for a buyer in Mexico, and in January 2024 forensic archaeologist Flavio Estrada presented the analysis at Peru’s Ministry of Culture: the figures were dolls built from human and animal bones glued with modern adhesive, “not extraterrestrials”.
properties.explanation: Forensic specialists working for Peru’s prosecutors and Ministry of Culture examined seized figures and found them to be three-fingered dolls assembled from human and animal bones held together with modern glue; similar bodies promoted in 2017 had already been found to be recently made.

properties.title: Colorado Springs law-enforcement videos
properties.shape: Silent lights flashing red, blue and green; triangle reports
properties.summary: The first local law-enforcement UAP files released by the U.S. government: cell-phone videos an officer submitted to AARO showing silent flashing lights, plus separate FBI interviews and renderings of triangle-shaped UAP seen over Colorado Springs in October 2023.
properties.explanation: Released by AARO/PURSUE as unresolved reports from a local law-enforcement officer; no determination published.

properties.title: Imphal airport UFO — Rafales scrambled
properties.place: Bir Tikendrajit International Airport, Imphal, Manipur
properties.shape: Small white object
properties.summary: An unidentified object seen near Imphal airport in the afternoon led the authorities to halt flights. Departures were delayed and arrivals diverted for about three hours. The Indian Air Force scrambled two Rafale fighters from a nearby base, which searched the area and found nothing. The object was not seen again.

properties.title: Langley Air Force Base drone incursions
properties.shape: Drones of several sizes; the first reportedly about 20 ft long
properties.summary: From the evening of December 6, 2023, unauthorized drones flew over Langley Air Force Base, home of F-22 Raptor squadrons, across Hampton Roads from the Navy’s largest base at Norfolk, on and off for 17 days. The Wall Street Journal later reported that they typically arrived 45 minutes to an hour after sunset, that the first was about 20 feet long and flew at 3,000 to 4,000 feet, and that a dozen or more smaller drones followed. The Pentagon confirmed the incursions in October 2024. Gen. Glen VanHerck, who led NORAD at the time, later said the military had warned for years that it was not ready for this threat; he gave no new details about who was operating the drones.
properties.explanation: The Pentagon confirmed the incursions in October 2024 and said the drones did not appear to show hostile intent, but neither it nor NORAD has said who flew them.

properties.title: Tyndall "Tic Tac" — USCG C-144
properties.place: Southeastern U.S., near Tyndall AFB, Florida
properties.shape: "Tic Tac" — IR-hot area of contrast
properties.summary: Two infrared clips titled "USCG C-144 Tyndall UAP … TIC TAC IR hot 24 April 2024", likely from a Coast Guard HC-144 sensor over the Southeastern United States, released in PURSUE Release 02 in response to a House request.
properties.explanation: AARO released the clips in 2026 as uploaded to a classified network, noting many of these records lack a substantiated chain of custody; no determination was made.

properties.title: The “plume” over Buenos Aires — a Chinese rocket identified
properties.place: Castelar, Buenos Aires province; also seen from Entre Ríos, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia and Paraguay
properties.shape: A glowing plume in an inverted V, rising across the sky
properties.summary: At about 11:30 p.m. on May 8, 2024, a man in Castelar, west of Buenos Aires, filmed a glowing, feather-shaped plume climbing across the sky for some forty minutes until it was almost overhead, and sent the video to the Argentine Air Force’s aerospace identification centre (CIAE). The same sight was reported that night from several Argentine provinces and from Paysandú in Uruguay, Valparaíso in Chile, Bolivia and Paraguay. The CIAE recognised the inverted-V pattern left by a rocket’s upper stage and found a Long March 3B/E that had lifted off from Xichang at 01:43 UTC on May 9 (22:43 in Argentina) with the Smart SkyNet 1-01 satellite. Rebuilding the ascent from its trajectory, it found the rocket over the South Pacific about 3,600 km up, heading north-east into the sector of sky the camera was pointing at, 47 minutes after launch. In its 2024 report the centre classed the case as definitely explained, like all 36 cases it analysed that year.
properties.explanation: Argentina’s Air Force identification centre (CIAE) matched the video, by the rocket’s ascent trajectory, to the exhaust plume of the Long March 3B/E launched 47 minutes earlier from Xichang, China, with the Smart SkyNet 1-01 satellite (NORAD catalogue number 59707); it classed the case “definitely explained”.

properties.title: The teardrop with a pole — United Arab Emirates
properties.shape: An inverted teardrop with a vertical bar or pole hanging below it
properties.summary: In June 2024 an infrared sensor aboard a U.S. military platform recorded 21 seconds of an object that looks like an inverted teardrop with a straight vertical mass hanging beneath it, held in the centre of the field of view throughout. The mission report described “an object with a vertical pole or bar attached to the bottom”, and the observer noted that it might be a reflection of something in the water. The video was reported to AARO and released on DVIDS in May 2026 as DOW-UAP-PR29, without a determination.
properties.explanation: AARO released it in 2026 as unresolved. The mission report (DoW-UAP-D8) describes an object with a vertical pole or bar under it, and the observer added that it might instead be a reflection from an object in the water.

properties.title: The “misshapen ball of white light” over Syria
properties.shape: A “misshapen and uneven ball of white light”, with white, red and orange patches on the video
properties.summary: In October 2024 a full-motion video camera aboard a U.S. military platform over Syria recorded what the mission report (DoW-UAP-D32) calls a “misshapen and uneven ball of white light”, adding that a “light/glare halo effect” appeared at the top of the feed. U.S. Central Command sent AARO three clips: in one an indistinct multi-coloured patch crosses the top edge of the display within a second; in another a half-oval of white and red highlights sits at the top edge; in the third two semi-transparent orange shapes overlay the picture for under two seconds each. They were released in May 2026 as DOW-UAP-PR31 to PR33.
properties.explanation: AARO released the three clips in 2026 as unresolved. The mission report itself notes a “light/glare halo effect” at the top of the video feed, and the clips last five or six seconds each, so an optical artefact cannot be excluded.

properties.title: The Yemen orb and the Hellfire — shown to Congress
properties.place: Off the coast of Yemen (exact location not released)
properties.shape: A bright orb, at moments more cylindrical, moving on a steady course
properties.summary: At a House Oversight hearing on UAP transparency on September 9, 2025, Rep. Eric Burlison showed a 50-second infrared clip he said came from a whistleblower and was taken on October 30, 2024 off the coast of Yemen. An MQ-9 Reaper tracks, and appears to laser-designate, a bright object moving on a steady path; a Hellfire missile fired by a second Reaper streaks in, appears to hit it and throw off fragments, and glances away without exploding, while the object carries on until the clip ends. Burlison would not speculate on what it was and said an independent review was under way; a defense official told The War Zone, “We do not have anything to provide on this.” The clip was also a rare public sign that Reapers were engaging aerial targets during the Houthi attacks on shipping.
properties.explanation: Unverified: the clip came from a whistleblower and the Pentagon has said nothing about it. Analysts suggested a Houthi cruise missile or drone, or a balloon, and noted that a Hellfire without a proximity fuse can pass through a light target without exploding.

properties.title: New Jersey drone sightings
properties.place: Morris County, New Jersey, and the Northeast
properties.shape: Large lighted drones; many reports were aircraft
properties.summary: From mid-November 2024, residents in Morris County reported large, lighted drones flying at night, including over Picatinny Arsenal and near the president-elect's golf club in Bedminster. Reports spread across New Jersey and into New York, Pennsylvania and beyond. The FAA placed temporary flight restrictions over dozens of sites. Stewart International Airport briefly closed its runways, and many viral videos turned out to show airliners.
properties.explanation: A joint FBI, DHS, FAA and DoD review found a mix of lawful commercial, hobbyist and law-enforcement drones, crewed aircraft and stars, with no threat to national security. In January 2025 the White House said the drones over New Jersey had been authorized by the FAA for research and other purposes.

properties.title: Drones over the U.S. air bases in England
properties.place: RAF Lakenheath, Mildenhall, Feltwell and Fairford, England
properties.shape: Small drones of varying number and type
properties.summary: Between November 20 and 26, 2024, small drones were seen over and around four bases in England used by the U.S. Air Force: RAF Lakenheath, home of the 48th Fighter Wing, RAF Mildenhall, RAF Feltwell and RAF Fairford. The Air Force said “small unmanned aerial systems were spotted in the vicinity of and over RAF Lakenheath, RAF Mildenhall and RAF Feltwell between 20 and 22 November”. Air traffic into Mildenhall was disrupted: on November 21 a KC-46 tanker that had brought F-35s across the Atlantic turned back and diverted to Prestwick. British troops with counter-drone equipment were sent to help, and the Ministry of Defence Police opened an inquiry. Similar reports came from U.S. bases in Germany that December.
properties.explanation: The U.S. Air Force and the Ministry of Defence confirmed the drones, and the Ministry of Defence Police opened an investigation, but the operators were not identified.

properties.title: Campo Largo — an influencer’s lights traced to a campsite
properties.shape: A ring of lights alternating in brightness above the trees
properties.summary: On May 31, 2026, Mayk Leão, a nursing technician and social-media influencer who lives alone on a remote farm in Campo Largo, Paraná, said his animals had been agitated, an electric fence was knocked down and he had heard metallic clicks, roars and mechanical noises; that evening he filmed bright lights in a circular group over a forested valley several kilometres away for twenty to forty minutes, and later drew a second, larger object he said passed over the property. His live streams and videos reached millions within days and drew national coverage. The Brazilian Air Force’s airspace department said its radars detected no unknown object, and internet users compared the sounds with a film trailer. Working from the coordinates of the farm, an image analyst then showed that the lights matched an escarpment beside a campsite, Chácara Paraíso, about 10 km away, whose lights are switched off when it has no guests.
properties.explanation: An image analyst who worked from the filming position showed the lights came from an escarpment by a campsite, Chácara Paraíso, about 10 km away, distorted by distance and the air; the campsite’s lights are off when it is empty, which is why they were not seen every night. The Brazilian Air Force said its air-defence radars detected nothing unusual.
